a1.RJF.label: fact

items.text: Raymond James' CEO describes the firm as offering the largest addressable market across its affiliation options, from employee to independent contractor to RIA custody, and notes advisors are coming from wires, regionals, and other independents; the value proposition of cultural fit, platform, and multiple affiliation options appeals to advisors from many firms.
items.quote: we have the largest addressable market across our affiliation options, from employee to independent contractor to the RIA custody, and we have critical mass and decades of experience in all of them... Advisors are coming from, you know, wires, regionals, other independents. And again, that value proposition... the cultural fit, the platform that I talked about, the multiple affiliation options, it's appealing to advisors from a lot of different firms.

items.text: The firm describes its differentiated value proposition as advisors not having to choose between culture and capabilities, offering a unique combination of an advisor- and client-focused culture with leading technology, products, and solutions.
items.quote: advisers do not have to choose between culture and capabilities. We offer a unique combination of an adviser and client-focused culture along with the leading technology, products and solutions advisers need to serve clients at a high level.

items.text: The firm states it does not lead with the highest check but leads with culture and capabilities, maintaining a differentiated value proposition and remaining disciplined on transition assistance and economics.
items.quote: we don't lead with the highest check. We want to have competitive economics... but we lead with culture and capabilities. And so we have a true differentiated value proposition. In the absence of a true differentiated value proposition, the highest check is all you have.

items.text: The firm describes its 'best-of-both-worlds' value proposition, combining an advisor- and client-focused culture with leading technology and solutions, and cites its strong balance sheet and commitment to independence as a differentiator for advisors evaluating alternatives.
items.quote: Our best-of-both-worlds value proposition, where we offer a unique combination of an advisor and client-focused culture coupled with leading technology and solutions, continues to resonate with advisors across all of our affiliation options. Additionally, our strong balance sheet and commitment to independence is proving to be a differentiator for advisors evaluating alternatives.

items.text: The CEO states the firm has the largest total addressable market by having all affiliation options at scale, so advisors moving do not have to consider whether Raymond James offers a channel but only whether they are a cultural fit.
items.quote: We have the largest total addressable market based on having all of the affiliation options at scale, and when advisors are thinking about making a move, they don't have to select. They don't have to think about whether or not Raymond James offers a channel... they can really just understand whether or not we're a good fit for them culturally in terms of the capabilities that we offer.

items.text: The firm states it has the largest addressable market because it has all affiliation options an advisor could want, and it is agnostic to how advisors affiliate, wanting them to embrace its culture, values, platform, and capabilities.
items.quote: we have the largest addressable market in the industry because we have all the affiliation options that an adviser could possibly want. And we have adviser choice where we're agnostic into how you affiliate with Raymond James. We want you to fall in love with our culture, values and the platform and capabilities.

items.text: The firm's recruiting pages describe the AdvisorChoice platform as offering advisors the ability to match professional goals to the affiliation option that is right for them, each backed by a leading independent financial firm.
items.quote: Through AdvisorChoice®, you have the ability to match your professional goals to the affiliation option that's right for you, each offering a unique combination of support, freedom and flexibility – and all backed by the full support of a leading independent financial firm.

a1.RJF.reason: The passages contain multiple explicit statements by the firm's CEO and recruiting materials describing its positioning to recruit advisors, including away from wirehouses, so these are facts.

items.text: Schwab has built its adviser business around helping independent advisers grow, compete and succeed, and continues to invest in the business to meet advisers' needs.
items.quote: We have built our adviser business around helping independent advisers grow, compete and succeed. ... We are continuing to invest in this business to meet advisers' needs.

items.text: According to Schwab, the RIA custody business requires scale, trust, operational excellence, outstanding service, and breadth to support advisers as their businesses and clients' needs become more complex.
items.quote: This business requires scale, trust, operational excellence, outstanding service and the breadth to support advisers as their businesses and their clients' needs become more complex.

items.text: Schwab is deepening relationships with the RIA firms it serves by building a broader support ecosystem that extends beyond custody alone to add value for RIAs.
items.quote: In our advisor services business, we're deepening relationships with the 16,000 RIA firms we serve by building a broader support ecosystem that extends beyond custody alone to add value for RIAs.

items.text: Schwab believes it can maintain its competitive position primarily through the efforts of its sales, support, technology, and business consulting teams, which are dedicated to helping RIAs grow, compete, and succeed.
items.quote: Management believes that we can maintain our competitive position primarily through the efforts of our sales, support, technology, and business consulting teams, which are dedicated to helping RIAs grow, compete, and succeed in serving their clients.

items.text: Schwab aims to be the leading RIA support ecosystem, providing wealth tools, investment/lending products, and technology in addition to custody and service.
items.quote: The leading RIA support ecosystem to help advisors serve their clients, providing wealth tools, investment / lending products, & technology in addition to custody & service

items.text: In advisor services, Schwab is adding support and capabilities for RIAs of all sizes while also helping new advisors transition to independence.
items.quote: In advisor services, we are adding support and capabilities for RIAs of all sizes while also helping new advisors transition to independence.

items.text: Schwab describes its offering as a differentiated, full-service platform built on scale and reputation, breadth beyond custody, operational excellence, and dedicated service and support.
items.quote: A differentiated, full-service platform ... Scale & Reputation 1 ... Breadth Beyond Custody ... Operational Excellence ... Dedicated Service & Support

items.text: Schwab will continue to focus on custody services for RIAs with under $100 million in AUM, positioning its role as providing a platform and support ecosystem to help advisors support their clients and help their firms thrive.
items.quote: Schwab will continue to focus on its custody services for registered investment advisors with under $100 million AUM ... "Our job and our role is to provide a platform and a support ecosystem that helps you support your clients and helps your firm thrive."

items.text: Schwab wants to give RIAs equal or better access than their wirehouse counterparts to banking services such as lending, private market investing, and long-short investment strategies, positioning itself as the RIA's bank.
items.quote: Schwab wants to give registered investment advisors equal or better access than their wirehouse counterparts to banking services such as lending , private market investing, and long-short investment strategies

items.text: Schwab's strategic priorities include broadening support for RIAs while improving monetization.

a1.MER.label: fact

items.text: Merrill grows its advisor force through an extensive training program and through experienced hiring of advisors; approximately one-third of net new households in Q2 2025 were added by newly trained advisors.
items.quote: We also continued to add financial advisors to the sales force in Merrill and the Private Bank through our extensive training program and experienced hiring of advisors. Approximately one-third of net new households in Q2 were added by our newly trained advisors.

items.text: Merrill's core advisor growth strategy is its training program that trains people in wealth management at Bank of America and Merrill; recruiting experienced advisors is also being picked up but is not an enormous part of the strategy.
items.quote: we're picking up the recruiting of experienced advisors. That isn't an enormous part of our strategy, but it's a training program so that we're training people in wealth management, Bank of America, and Merrill, and that's ultimately what we believe we can just keep driving in order to improve the net new flows.

items.text: Merrill develops advisors through the Advisor Development Program, a structured path that progresses through roles (Client Associate, Financial Solutions Advisor, Financial Advisor) and graduates advisors to Merrill Core Advisor, designed to help advisors build a book of high-net-worth clients.
items.quote: Roles are designed to enhance your ability to meet and help clients identify financial goals, align banking and investing solutions and build your book of high-net worth clients.

items.text: Merrill's foundational belief for its wealth business includes that having the best advisors enables it to deliver exceptional client outcomes.
items.quote: having the best advisors enables us to deliver exceptional client outcomes

items.text: Merrill returned to veteran broker recruiting after largely pulling back at the end of 2017; the firm restored a focus on hiring and a more aggressive offer under Co-Presidents Lindsay Hans and Eric Schimpf, who took over in 2023, and recruited assets doubled year-over-year.
items.quote: Merrill executives in October touted that recruited assets to the wealth unit doubled year-over-year as the firm has returned to veteran broker recruiting. The firm largely pulled back from veteran broker recruiting at the end of 2017 but returned after Co-Presidents Lindsay Hans and Eric Schimpf, who took over in 2023, restored a focus on hiring and a more aggressive offer.

a1.MER.reason: Multiple passages directly state Merrill's advisor growth strategy: a training program (Advisor Development Program) plus experienced/veteran advisor recruiting, with the training program being the central component.

a2.MER.label: fact

items.text: CFO Borthwick describes the advisor growth strategy as continuing to grow the sales force, referencing the 'Merrill 5% guide' of aiming for 5% growth over the next 3 to 5 years, and notes advisor attrition is now at near historic lows.
items.quote: we said we are aiming for 5% over the course of the next 3 to 5 years... I think what Lindsay and Eric are trying to drive there, what Katy is trying to drive there is just keep growing the sales force. Well, adviser attrition is now at near historic lows.

items.text: CFO Borthwick describes the advisor growth strategy as primarily a training program (training people in wealth management at Bank of America and Merrill), supplemented by recruiting experienced advisors which 'isn't an enormous part' of the strategy.
items.quote: we're picking up the recruiting of experienced advisors. That isn't an enormous part of our strategy, but it's a training program so that we're training people in wealth management, Bank of America, and Merrill, and that's ultimately what we believe we can just keep driving in order to improve the net new flows.

items.quote: We also continued to add financial advisors to the sales force in Merrill and the Private Bank through our extensive training program and experienced hiring of advisors.

a1.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley says it is making ongoing investments in its world-class platform, including investments to support its advisors, a build-out of E*TRADE capabilities, and the expansion of its workplace channel.
items.quote: Ongoing investments in our world-class platform, including investments to support our advisors, a build-out of E*TRADE capabilities, and the expansion of our essential workplace channel, serve as an engine for future growth.

items.text: Morgan Stanley names LeadIQ, its AI-powered lead distribution platform, which focuses on matching workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitating engagement with its financial advisors, as one of its early AI use cases.
items.quote: LeadIQ, our AI-powered lead distribution platform, focusing on matching workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitating engagement with our financial advisors.

items.text: Morgan Stanley names Parable, an interactive tool that quickly analyzes and summarizes data, as one of its early AI use cases.
items.quote: Parable, an interactive tool that quickly analyzes and summarizes data

items.text: Morgan Stanley names the DevGen AI tool, which enhances developer efficiency by modernizing code, as one of its early AI use cases.
items.quote: the DevGen AI tool, which enhances developer efficiency by modernizing code

items.text: Morgan Stanley states that its scale supports continued investment in future technology, including AI and digital tools.
items.quote: our scale supports continued investment in future technology, including AI and digital tools.

items.text: Morgan Stanley states it continues to invest in deepening its competitive moats in areas such as its expanded collaboration with Carta in private markets and in digital assets through announced partnerships with Zero Hash.
items.quote: we continue to invest, deepening our competitive moats in areas like our expanded collaboration with Carta in private markets and in digital assets through announced partnerships with Zero Hash.

items.text: Morgan Stanley states it has put significant resources toward lending products, including digital tools, digital enhancements, and using automation to help with the paper backlog associated with various lending products.
items.quote: we've put in a lot of resources towards lending products more broadly. So digital tools, digital enhancements and using automation to be able to help with the paper backlog associated with some of the various lending products more broadly.

items.text: Morgan Stanley states it was overweighted to AI from the early days in wealth, including some of the work it did with OpenAI.
items.quote: We were, as you know, overweighted to AI from the early days in wealth with some of the work we did with OpenAI.

items.text: Morgan Stanley states that the insights from its size and scale allow its financial advisors to tailor advice and equip its own tools to deliver that advice to help clients achieve their goals.
items.quote: It gives us insights given our size and scale that allow our FAs to tailor advice and equip our own tools to deliver that advice to help clients achieve their goals.

items.text: Morgan Stanley states it continues to invest across its technology stack, embracing AI tools to support its infrastructure, business growth and people.
items.quote: We continue to invest across our technology stack, embracing AI tools to support our infrastructure, business growth and people.

items.text: Morgan Stanley states it has been investing in its processes and systems across the technology side, in better understanding its data, and in better servicing its clients.
items.quote: we've been investing in all of our processes and our systems in order to engage and make sure that we have a robust infrastructure... that has to do with everything that I mentioned across the technology side, across better understanding our data, better servicing our clients.

a1.MS.reason: Multiple passages state specific areas where Morgan Stanley is investing in technology, including AI tools for advisors, platform investments, digital tools for lending, private markets and digital assets.

a4.MS.label: fact

items.text: CEO Edward Pick describes AI as a top priority for the firm's advisory role, saying the firm is now 'double overweight' on AI and that it is existentially important that Morgan Stanley be viewed as a trusted adviser in the middle of the ecosystem.
items.quote: There is just no question that this is existentially important that we are viewed as a trusted adviser in the middle of the ecosystem... And for us to be part of the content and the thinking and the evolution of this is absolutely the top priority for the firm as the adviser

items.text: CFO Sharon Yeshaya describes early AI use cases, including LeadIQ, 'our AI-powered lead distribution platform, focusing on matching workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitating engagement with our financial advisors,' as well as DevGen AI (enhancing developer efficiency) and Parable (an interactive tool analyzing and summarizing data).
items.quote: LeadIQ, our AI-powered lead distribution platform, focusing on matching workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitating engagement with our financial advisors.

items.text: CFO Sharon Yeshaya states the firm's scale 'supports continued investment in future technology, including AI and digital tools.'
items.quote: while our scale supports continued investment in future technology, including AI and digital tools.

items.text: CEO Ted Pick states the firm is using its scale to invest in broadening capabilities for financial advisors that are difficult for others to replicate, including alternatives and privates, tax-efficient investing, digitized assets, family office and OCIO, and tailored lending.
items.quote: We are using our scale to invest in broadening capabilities for FAs that are difficult for others to replicate: alternatives and privates, tax-efficient investing, digitized assets, family office and OCIO, and tailored lending.

items.text: CEO Edward Pick describes the ability to protect client assets and a resiliency theme as critical to clients, and states that although it is a people business, technology can help do a lot of the early work for financial advisers.
items.quote: the ability to protect client assets... there will be a resiliency theme that will be super important to clients with real net worth... that is something that technology can help do a lot of the early work.

items.text: CEO Edward Pick describes the firm's 'world-class technology, world-class cyber defense and then the best trusted advisers sitting with the client' as the 'secret sauce,' including for the wealth management and financial adviser.
items.quote: this is something we consider to be additive to what we have, which is world-class technology, world-class cyber defense and then the best trusted advisers sitting with the client.

items.text: CEO Ted Pick states the firm continues to invest in Wealth, Institutional Securities, and Investment Management via human capital and technology, with growth plans embedding increasing adoption of AI tools throughout the enterprise and client base.
items.quote: We continue to invest in each of our three business segments: Wealth, Institutional Securities, and Investment Management via human capital and technology. Our growth plans embed the increasing adoption of AI tools throughout the enterprise and inside our client base.

items.text: CFO Sharon Yeshaya states the firm continues to invest across its technology stack, embracing AI tools to support its infrastructure, business growth and people.
items.quote: We continue to invest across our technology stack, embracing AI tools to support our infrastructure, business growth and people.

items.text: CEO Edward Pick states cyber resiliency is a top priority across all of the firm's businesses, and that AI will bring efficiency and effectiveness that should not be dismissed as it transforms the firm.
items.quote: cyber resiliency is a top priority at institutions like ours across all of our businesses... a lot of the good that AI is going to bring both as an efficiency and effectiveness matter should not get dismissed

items.text: CEO Edward Pick states the firm has built advantages against its advisor-led platform that make technology a differentiator in its favor.
items.quote: we have built a number of advantages that not only allow us to preserve our moat, but actually make technology a differentiator in our favor.

items.text: CEO Ted Pick describes the early digital asset transformation in wealth, including a partnership with Zero Hash, expansion into crypto and tokenized asset capabilities, and continued work on the E*TRADE platform for the active self-directed community.
items.quote: the early days of the digital asset transformation side of wealth. We announced a partnership with Zero Hash last year... well positioned now in the crypto and tokenized asset space... continued work that we're doing in E*TRADE

a1.RJF.label: fact

items.text: Raymond James offers multiple affiliation options, which it refers to as AdvisorChoice®.
items.quote: We offer multiple affiliation options, which we refer to as AdvisorChoice®.

items.text: Financial advisors primarily affiliate with Raymond James directly as either employees or independent contractors, or as employees of third-party Registered Investment Advisors (RIAs) and broker-dealers served through the RIA and Custody Services (RCS) division.
items.quote: Financial advisors primarily affiliate with us directly as either employees or independent contractors or as employees of third-party Registered Investment Advisors (“RIAs”) and broker-dealers to which we provide services through our RIA and Custody Services (“RCS”) division.

items.text: Employee financial advisors work in a traditional branch supported by local management and administrative staff, and serve predominantly retail clients.
items.quote: Employee financial advisors work in a traditional branch supported by local management and administrative staff. They provide services predominantly to retail clients.

items.text: Raymond James describes its AdvisorChoice affiliation options as Traditional Employee, Advisor Select, Independent Contractor, Bank & Credit Union, and Corporate RIA.
items.quote: Traditional Employee: Get everything you expect from working for a firm with a powerful difference – book ownership. Advisor Select: Lead your own branch... Independent Contractor: Operate as an independent financial advisor... Bank & Credit Union: Leverage national strength and local impact... Corporate RIA: Exercise true autonomy...

items.text: Raymond James describes its affiliation spectrum as spanning Employee Advisor (RJA), Advisor Select, Independent Advisor (ICD), Banks and Credit Unions, IAR (Corporate RIA), and RIA & Custody Services, noting that 'the movement to independence is not channel-specific.'
items.quote: EMPLOYEE ADVISOR (RJA) | ADVISOR SELECT | INDEPENDENT ADVISOR (ICD) | BANKS AND CREDIT UNIONS | IAR* (CORPORATE RIA) | RIA** & CUSTODY SERVICES. The movement to "independence" is not channel-specific

items.text: Independent contractor financial advisors are generally responsible for their direct costs and accordingly receive a higher payout percentage than employee financial advisors; they may affiliate directly or through an affiliated bank or credit union in the Financial Institutions Division.
items.quote: Our financial advisors who are independent contractors are generally responsible for all of their direct costs and, accordingly, receive a higher payout percentage on the revenues they generate than employee financial advisors.

items.text: Through its domestic RCS division, Raymond James offers third-party RIAs and broker-dealers custodial services, trade execution, research and other support; financial advisors associated with RCS firms are not included in Raymond James' advisor counts.
items.quote: Through our domestic RCS division, we offer third-party RIAs and broker-dealers a range of products and services including custodial services, trade execution, research, and other support and services... Financial advisors associated with firms in RCS are not included in our financial advisor counts

items.text: Raymond James says it is agnostic about how advisors affiliate, offering all the affiliation options and therefore the largest addressable market in the industry.
items.quote: we have the largest addressable market in the industry because we have all the affiliation options that an adviser could possibly want. And we have adviser choice where we're agnostic into how you affiliate with Raymond James.

items.text: Raymond James says it has the largest addressable market across its affiliation options—employee, independent contractor, and RIA custody—with critical mass and decades of experience in each, and that it is not a new venture for the firm.
items.quote: we have the largest addressable market across our affiliation options, from employee to independent contractor to the RIA custody, and we have critical mass and decades of experience in all of them. It's not a new venture for us.

items.text: On the affiliation mix, CEO Paul Reilly said RCS has by far the highest percentage growth, while this year the employee channel led the way; he expected some improvement in the independent contractor model.
items.quote: In our RIA part, RCS, it is by far the highest percentage growth... This year, the employee channel really led the way... I actually think that we'll get some improvement in the independent contractor model because it's just cyclical

items.text: Raymond James says the acceleration rate within the independent channel is probably higher, while still seeing success in the employee affiliation option and the independent RIA option.
items.quote: Certainly, the acceleration rate within the independent channel is probably higher, but we are still seeing very good success in the employee affiliation option and the independent RIA, option as well.

items.text: Recruiting activity is broad-based across affiliation options but has been more heavily tilted toward the independent contractor side in the last six months.
items.quote: the recruiting activity is robust. It's broad-based across our affiliation options, maybe more heavily tilted in the last six months on the independent contractor side of the business.

items.text: Raymond James is seeing a good uptick in the employee affiliation option, and describes the mix shift as relating to the comp ratio because of the payout difference between the independent and employee channels.
items.quote: we're actually seeing pretty good uptick in the employee affiliation option as well. And the mix shift is really what I was referring to more about the comp ratio than the margin because the payout difference in the independent channel versus the employee channel.

items.text: The affiliation options differ in how advisors spend their time day-to-day: the employee option suits those focused on building their books of business, while others want to run a business including building a team, paying benefits, and dealing with real estate and legal aspects.
items.quote: Some want to dedicate as close to possible as 100% of their time building their books of business, serving their clients... that's more aligned with the employee affiliation option and some want to run a business on -- in addition to those responsibilities... running a business.

items.text: Recruiting success is spread across all affiliation channels; the independent contractor channel is seeing the most interest in dollar volume, while the RIA custody division is growing at a high percentage rate on a smaller base.
items.quote: Shoukry said the firm's recruiting success is spread across all its affiliation channels, including its RIA custody channel. The independent contractor channel is seeing the most interest in terms of dollar volume. "But the RIA custody division on a smaller base is growing at a high percentage rate as well"

a1.RJF.reason: The passages contain multiple direct statements from Raymond James describing its affiliation models (AdvisorChoice, employee/independent contractor/RCS) and how the mix across them has shifted.

a2.RJF.label: fact

items.text: Raymond James states it has the largest addressable market in the industry because it offers all the affiliation options an advisor could want, and it is 'agnostic' about how an advisor affiliates, wanting advisors to fall in love with its culture, values, platform and capabilities.
items.quote: we have the largest addressable market in the industry because we have all the affiliation options that an adviser could possibly want. And we have adviser choice where we're agnostic into how you affiliate with Raymond James. We want you to fall in love with our culture, values and the platform and capabilities and how you affiliate with us, we're indifferent to.

items.text: Raymond James describes its multiple affiliation options collectively as 'AdvisorChoice', offered to financial advisors who primarily affiliate directly as employees or independent contractors, or as employees of third-party RIAs and broker-dealers served through its RIA and Custody Services (RCS) division.
items.quote: We offer multiple affiliation options, which we refer to as AdvisorChoice®. Financial advisors primarily affiliate with us directly as either employees or independent contractors or as employees of third-party Registered Investment Advisors ("RIAs") and broker-dealers to which we provide services through our RIA and Custody Services ("RCS") division.

items.text: Through AdvisorChoice, Raymond James says advisors can match their professional goals to the affiliation option that is right for them, each offering a unique combination of support, freedom and flexibility backed by the full support of a leading independent financial firm.
items.quote: Through AdvisorChoice®, you have the ability to match your professional goals to the affiliation option that's right for you, each offering a unique combination of support, freedom and flexibility – and all backed by the full support of a leading independent financial firm.

items.text: Raymond James describes its 'best of both worlds' value proposition as a unique combination of an advisor- and client-focused culture coupled with leading technology and solutions, which it says resonates with advisors across all its affiliation options.
items.quote: Our best of both worlds value proposition, where we offer a unique combination of an advisor and client-focused culture coupled with leading technology and solutions, continues to resonate with advisors across all of our affiliation options.

items.text: Raymond James lists its value proposition pillars as a service-first culture, respect for financial advisor independence, and a comprehensive and growing product and solution set.
items.quote: Service 1 st Culture / Respect for Financial Advisor Independence / Comprehensive and Growing Product & Solution Set

items.text: Raymond James says its affiliation strategy lets advisors not have to choose between culture and capabilities, offering an advisor- and client-focused culture along with leading technology, products and solutions.
items.quote: advisers do not have to choose between culture and capabilities. We offer a unique combination of an adviser and client-focused culture along with the leading technology, products and solutions advisers need to serve clients at a high level.

items.text: Raymond James says its independent contractor advisor options are designed to help advisors build their businesses with as much or as little of its support as they determine they need.
items.quote: Our independent contractor financial advisor options are designed to help our advisors build their businesses with as much or as little of our support as they determine they need.

items.text: Raymond James describes its mission for the affiliation models as to inspire and empower the world's best financial professionals, tied to multiple affiliation options, 'best of both worlds,' advisor and book ownership, and RJF stability.
items.quote: Multiple Affiliation Options / Best of Both Worlds / Advisor and Book Ownership / RJF Stability / Inspire and empower the world's best financial professionals.

a2.RJF.reason: The passages directly state Raymond James's stated priorities and strategy behind its affiliation models, including AdvisorChoice, agnosticism across channels, the best-of-both-worlds value proposition, and its value-proposition pillars.

a3.RJF.label: fact

items.text: Raymond James states it competes directly with national full service broker-dealers, investment banking firms, commercial banks, investment advisors, investment managers and, to a lesser extent, discount brokers and dealers, and faces competition from newer entrants including fintechs, as well as indirect competition for investment assets from insurance companies, real estate firms and hedge funds.
items.quote: We compete directly with other national full service broker-dealers, investment banking firms, commercial banks, investment advisors, investment managers and, to a lesser extent, discount brokers and dealers. We face competition from more recent entrants into the market, including fintechs... We also compete indirectly for investment assets with insurance companies, real estate firms, and hedge funds, among others.

items.text: Raymond James says the continued industry-wide trend of financial advisors departing traditional firms, including to form independent RIAs or join existing third-party RIAs some of which are backed by private equity investors, has resulted in a highly competitive recruiting environment.
items.quote: Our PCG business is subject to risks arising from the continued industry-wide trend in which financial advisors are departing traditional firms, including to form independent RIAs or to join existing third-party RIAs, some of which are backed by private equity investors. This ongoing trend has resulted in a highly competitive recruiting environment.

items.text: Raymond James says many of its competitors are increasingly looking for an exit in three to five years or less, many compete with the largest check, and many change their comp plans every year to cross-sell more bank products.
items.quote: whereas so many of our competitors are increasingly looking for an exit in three to five years or even less... whereas many of our competitors compete with the largest check... whereas many of our competitors change their comp plans every year to cross-sell more bank products.

items.text: Raymond James names PE-backed roll-ups as a relatively novel competitive dynamic, saying they have been extremely aggressive in paying higher and higher multiples for advisors over the last three years.
items.quote: The dynamic that's relatively novel in the last five years is these PE-backed roll-ups cropping up everywhere. Over the last three years in particular, they've been extremely aggressive in trading and paying at higher and higher multiples.

items.text: Raymond James says it still sees pressure on the existing advisor base from private equity roll-ups, which in the absence of a value proposition compete with big checks.
items.quote: We are still seeing pressure on the existing advisor base, private equity. We always say with the roll-ups, in the absence of a value proposition, they compete with big checks.

items.text: Raymond James says there are more competitive pressures now with private equity-backed roll-ups and that sort of thing.
items.quote: Yeah, there are more competitive pressures now with private equity-backed roll-ups and that sort of thing.

items.text: Raymond James says many competitors that focus on personal relationships and have similar cultures invest only a fraction of what it does in technology, making it hard for them to remain competitive.
items.quote: a lot of our competitors who also are focused on personal relationships, and that have similar cultures, their technology investment, for example, is a fraction of ours. And that's hard to remain in competitive when you can't invest in AI and the tools that you need

items.text: Raymond James says competitors that lack a true differentiated value proposition lead with the highest check.
items.quote: We don't lead with the highest check... In the absence of a true differentiated value proposition, the highest check is all you have.

items.text: Raymond James says advisors are coming to it from a lot of different competitor firms, including wirehouses, regionals and other independents.
items.quote: Advisors are coming from, you know, wires, regionals, other independents.

items.text: Raymond James says private equity has certainly been competitive over the last five years, as well as some of the strategic firms.
items.quote: Private equity has certainly been competitive over the last 5 years as well as some of the strategic firms.

items.text: Raymond James notes it is possible that certain of its competitors will withdraw from the Protocol for Broker Recruiting, which governs the client information advisors may take when they affiliate with a new firm.
items.quote: Participation in the Protocol is voluntary, and it is possible that certain of our competitors will withdraw from it.

a3.RJF.reason: The passages name competitors Raymond James faces around its affiliation models and advisor recruiting, which is what the sub-question asks.

items.text: Raymond James' CEO said that over the last year, in particular, much more of its advisor recruiting has come from the independent side of the business versus the employee side, representing a mix shift.
items.quote: over the last year, in particular, much more of our recruiting has come from the independent side of the business versus the employee side of the business. So there's just a mix shift there to some extent that you're looking at over the last year or so.

items.text: Raymond James' CEO said the firm is seeing a good uptick in the employee affiliation option, and that the mix shift he referenced concerns the compensation ratio (not margin), because of the payout difference between the independent and employee channels.

claims.text: Raymond James Financial: Raymond James offers multiple affiliation options, which it refers to as AdvisorChoice®.
Raymond James Financial: Employee financial advisors work in a traditional branch supported by local management and administrative staff, and serve predominantly retail clients.
Raymond James Financial: Raymond James describes its AdvisorChoice affiliation options as Traditional Employee, Advisor Select, Independent Contractor, Bank & Credit Union, and Corporate RIA.
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]

claims.text: Raymond James Financial: Raymond James describes its affiliation spectrum as spanning Employee Advisor (RJA), Advisor Select, Independent Advisor (ICD), Banks and Credit Unions, IAR (Corporate RIA), and RIA & Custody Services, noting that the movement to independence is not channel-specific.

Raymond James Financial: Independent contractor financial advisors are generally responsible for their direct costs and accordingly receive a higher payout percentage than employee financial advisors; they may affiliate directly or through an affiliated bank or credit union in the Financial Institutions Division.

Raymond James Financial: Through its domestic RCS division, Raymond James offers third-party RIAs and broker-dealers custodial services, trade execution, research and other support; financial advisors associated with RCS firms are not included in Raymond James' advisor counts.
Raymond James Financial: Raymond James says it is agnostic about how advisors affiliate, offering all the affiliation options and therefore the largest addressable market in the industry.

Raymond James Financial: Raymond James says it has the largest addressable market across its affiliation options—employee, independent contractor, and RIA custody—with critical mass and decades of experience in each, and that it is not a new venture for the firm.

Raymond James Financial: On the affiliation mix, CEO Paul Reilly said RCS has by far the highest percentage growth, while this year the employee channel led the way; he expected some improvement in the independent contractor model.

Raymond James Financial: Raymond James says the acceleration rate within the independent channel is probably higher, while still seeing success in the employee affiliation option and the independent RIA option.
Raymond James Financial: Recruiting activity is broad-based across affiliation options but has been more heavily tilted toward the independent contractor side in the last six months.

Raymond James Financial: Raymond James is seeing a good uptick in the employee affiliation option, and describes the mix shift as relating to the comp ratio because of the payout difference between the independent and employee channels.

Raymond James Financial: The affiliation options differ in how advisors spend their time day-to-day: the employee option suits those focused on building their books of business, while others want to run a business including building a team, paying benefits, and dealing with real estate and legal aspects.

Raymond James Financial: Recruiting success is spread across all affiliation channels; the independent contractor channel is seeing the most interest in dollar volume, while the RIA custody division is growing at a high percentage rate on a smaller base.

Raymond James Financial: Raymond James states it has the largest addressable market in the industry because it offers all the affiliation options an advisor could want, and it is agnostic about how an advisor affiliates, wanting advisors to fall in love with its culture, values, platform and capabilities.

Raymond James Financial: Raymond James describes its multiple affiliation options collectively as AdvisorChoice, offered to financial advisors who primarily affiliate directly as employees or independent contractors, or as employees of third-party RIAs and broker-dealers served through its RIA and Custody Services (RCS) division.

Raymond James Financial: Through AdvisorChoice, Raymond James says advisors can match their professional goals to the affiliation option that is right for them, each offering a unique combination of support, freedom and flexibility backed by the full support of a leading independent financial firm.
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]

claims.text: Raymond James Financial: Raymond James describes its best of both worlds value proposition as a unique combination of an advisor- and client-focused culture coupled with leading technology and solutions, which it says resonates with advisors across all its affiliation options.

Raymond James Financial: Raymond James lists its value proposition pillars as a service-first culture, respect for financial advisor independence, and a comprehensive and growing product and solution set.

Raymond James Financial: Raymond James says its affiliation strategy lets advisors not have to choose between culture and capabilities, offering an advisor- and client-focused culture along with leading technology, products and solutions.

Raymond James Financial: Raymond James says its independent contractor advisor options are designed to help advisors build their businesses with as much or as little of its support as they determine they need.

Raymond James Financial: Raymond James describes its mission for the affiliation models as to inspire and empower the world's best financial professionals, tied to multiple affiliation options, best of both worlds, advisor and book ownership, and RJF stability.

Raymond James Financial: Raymond James states it competes directly with national full service broker-dealers, investment banking firms, commercial banks, investment advisors, investment managers and, to a lesser extent, discount brokers and dealers, and faces competition from newer entrants including fintechs, as well as indirect competition for investment assets from insurance companies, real estate firms and hedge funds.

Raymond James Financial: Raymond James says the continued industry-wide trend of financial advisors departing traditional firms, including to form independent RIAs or join existing third-party RIAs some of which are backed by private equity investors, has resulted in a highly competitive recruiting environment.

Raymond James Financial: Raymond James says many of its competitors are increasingly looking for an exit in three to five years or less, many compete with the largest check, and many change their comp plans every year to cross-sell more bank products.

Raymond James Financial: Raymond James names PE-backed roll-ups as a relatively novel competitive dynamic, saying they have been extremely aggressive in paying higher and higher multiples for advisors over the last three years.
Raymond James Financial: Raymond James says it still sees pressure on the existing advisor base from private equity roll-ups, which in the absence of a value proposition compete with big checks.
Raymond James Financial: Raymond James says there are more competitive pressures now with private equity-backed roll-ups and that sort of thing.

Raymond James Financial: Raymond James says many competitors that focus on personal relationships and have similar cultures invest only a fraction of what it does in technology, making it hard for them to remain competitive.
Raymond James Financial: Raymond James says competitors that lack a true differentiated value proposition lead with the highest check.
Raymond James Financial: Raymond James says advisors are coming to it from a lot of different competitor firms, including wirehouses, regionals and other independents.
Raymond James Financial: Raymond James says private equity has certainly been competitive over the last five years, as well as some of the strategic firms.

Raymond James Financial: Raymond James notes it is possible that certain of its competitors will withdraw from the Protocol for Broker Recruiting, which governs the client information advisors may take when they affiliate with a new firm.

Raymond James Financial: Paul Shoukry stated that over the last year much more of Raymond James's recruiting has come from the independent side of the business versus the employee side, indicating a mix shift toward independent.

Raymond James Financial: Paul Reilly stated that RCS is by far the highest percentage growth, and in total dollars the employee channel led the way this fiscal year (2024), whereas a couple of years ago it was the independent channel.

Raymond James Financial: Whether the mix across Raymond James affiliation models has shifted over time can be reported on this evidence, but only descriptively from management and trade-press statements rather than from one continuous series: the headcount and AUA figures in the matrix sit on different bases and different periods (whole-firm headcount at September 30 of 2023–2025; affiliation-model AUA at March 31 of 2020 and 2025; RCS-division AUA at various quarter-ends from 2025 to 2026), so they are not comparable as a single mix series. Management's own statements (RJF-TR-2024Q3#66, RJF-TR-2026Q1#44, RJF-TR-2026Q1#46, RJF-TRADE-2026-10-29-WM-01#0) do describe shifts over time and are cited under aspect a6.

a1.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley recruits financial advisors through its advisor-led channel, while also receiving flows into that channel from its workplace funnel.
items.quote: From the advisor-led side, we do have recruiting, but we also have flows coming in from workplace.

items.text: The firm attributes advisor recruiting interest to the platform it has invested in: 'There's obviously a great platform. We have recruits that are interested in what we've been investing in.'
items.quote: There's obviously a great platform. We have recruits that are interested in what we've been investing in.

items.text: Advisor recruitment remains strong, which the firm attributes to its reputation as an exceptional place where financial advisors can grow their businesses.
items.quote: Advisor recruitment remains strong, reflecting our reputation as an exceptional place where financial advisors can grow their businesses.

items.text: The firm attracts advisors by offering unique access to intellectual capital, world-class technology and compensation viewed as fair and motivating, and it is selective about recruiting.
items.quote: the financial advisor is seeing the integrated firm for what it is, which is we can offer unique access to intellectual capital, world-class technology, compensation that is viewed to be fair and motivating, and the entire thing works. What is happening is we are selective about it

items.text: The firm grants employee loans under a program established primarily to recruit certain Wealth Management financial advisors; these loans are full recourse, generally require periodic repayments, and are due in full upon termination of employment.
items.quote: Employee loans are granted in conjunction with a program established primarily to recruit certain Wealth Management financial advisors, are full recourse and generally require periodic repayments, and are due in full upon termination of employment with the Firm.

a1.MS.reason: Multiple passages directly state how the firm approaches advisor recruiting: recruiting from the advisor-led channel supplemented by workplace flows, the appeal of its platform, its reputation for advisor growth, its integrated-firm offerings and selectivity, and its use of recruiting employee loans.

a2.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley grants employee loans under a program established primarily to recruit certain Wealth Management financial advisors.
items.quote: Employee loans are granted in conjunction with a program established primarily to recruit certain Wealth Management financial advisors, are full recourse and generally require periodic repayments, and are due in full upon termination of employment with the Firm.

items.text: Morgan Stanley's advisor-led asset flows were particularly strong, originating from new advisors attracted to the strength of the workplace.
items.quote: Advisor-led flows were particularly strong, originating from new advisors who are attracted to the strength of the workplace, as well as assets that originated from workplace.

items.text: Morgan Stanley's advisor-led channel is coming from existing advisors as well as from recruits.
items.quote: Advisor-led is coming both from existing advisors as well as recruits and the origination of workplace.

items.text: Morgan Stanley has recruits interested in what it has been investing in, and does have recruiting on the advisor-led side.
items.quote: There's obviously a great platform. We have recruits that are interested in what we've been investing in... From the advisor-led side, we do have recruiting, but we also have flows coming in from workplace.

items.text: Morgan Stanley is selective in recruiting but is receiving a lot of inbound inquiry from financial advisors wanting to join the platform.
items.quote: What is happening is we are selective about it, but it is fair to say that Jed and Vince are getting a lot of inbound inquiry, and we would expect that to continue.

items.text: Advisor recruitment at Morgan Stanley remains strong, reflecting its reputation as an exceptional place where financial advisors can grow their businesses.
items.quote: Advisor recruitment remains strong, reflecting our reputation as an exceptional place where financial advisors can grow their businesses.

items.text: Morgan Stanley is seeing advisor-led asset flows from the recruiting side.
items.quote: On the advisor-led side, it is multiple clients and multiple different sections that you are actually seeing those flows come in, and we are also seeing flows from the recruiting side.

a2.MS.reason: Multiple passages describe whom Morgan Stanley recruits: experienced financial advisors (via a recruiting loan program), new advisors/recruits, and existing advisors, so these are facts about the target of recruiting.

a3.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley states that employee loans are granted under a program established primarily to recruit certain Wealth Management financial advisors; the loans are full recourse, generally require periodic repayments, and are due in full upon termination of employment.
items.quote: Employee loans are granted in conjunction with a program established primarily to recruit certain Wealth Management financial advisors, are full recourse and generally require periodic repayments, and are due in full upon termination of employment with the Firm.

items.text: Morgan Stanley sought to claw back $2.46 million in recruiting bonus loans (along with attorney's fees and interest) from a financial advisor, indicating the firm provides recruiting bonus loans to advisors.
items.quote: Morgan Stanley's attempt to claw back $2.46 million in recruiting bonus loans, along with attorney's fees and interest.

items.text: Morgan Stanley sought to claw back recruiting bonus money from a former advisor in a dispute over promissory notes, described as loans that brokers pay back to firms over time.
items.quote: Morgan Stanley sought to claw back recruiting bonus money from Cohen... in a dispute over promissory notes, loans that brokers pay back to firms over time.

items.text: Morgan Stanley is not introducing retention bonuses in its 2027 advisor pay plan; instead it is increasing a pay threshold for advisors by 10% in 2027, requiring advisors to generate that much more revenue to receive the same pay.
items.quote: Morgan Stanley and Merrill Lynch are not introducing retention bonuses as part of their 2027 pay plans for advisors... items.text: Raymond James offers multiple affiliation options, referred to as AdvisorChoice®, through which financial advisors affiliate as employees, independent contractors, or as employees of third-party RIAs and broker-dealers served through its RIA and Custody Services division.
items.quote: We offer multiple affiliation options, which we refer to as AdvisorChoice®. Financial advisors primarily affiliate with us directly as either employees or independent contractors or as employees of third-party Registered Investment Advisors (“RIAs”) and broker-dealers to which we provide services through our RIA and Custody Services (“RCS”) division.

items.text: Raymond James prefers to recruit advisors one-by-one rather than through acquisitions, because 100% of transition assistance goes to retention of the advisor and it can ensure advisors are a good cultural fit.
items.quote: So we prefer to recruit 1 by 1 versus doing acquisitions because we know -- first, 100% of the transition assistance is going to retention of the adviser. And secondly, we can ensure that the advisers we're bringing over a really good cultural fits for the firm.

items.text: Raymond James offers loans to financial advisors for recruiting and retention purposes, generally repaid over five-to-ten years and contingent upon continued affiliation.
items.quote: We offer loans to financial advisors for recruiting and retention purposes. The decision to extend credit to a financial advisor is generally based on their ability to generate future revenues. Loans offered are generally repaid over a five -to- ten year period, with interest recognized as earned, and are contingent upon continued affiliation with us.

items.text: Raymond James's culture is rooted in values it pledges to clients, advisors and associates: put clients first, act with integrity, think long term, and value independence.
items.quote: Our pledge to clients, to our advisors, and to all of our associates is that: • we put clients first, • we act with integrity, • we think long term, and • we value independence.

items.text: Raymond James's advisor retention philosophy is to retain before it recruits.
items.quote: it goes back to how we think about adviser retention. You have to retain before you recruit.

items.text: Raymond James states it attracts and retains advisors with its culture, service and platform, whereas many competitors compete with the largest financial package.
items.quote: We attract and retain financial advisors with our unique culture, leading service, and robust platform, whereas many of our competitors compete with the largest check.

items.text: Raymond James participates, with limited exceptions, in the Protocol for Broker Recruiting, which governs the client information advisors may take when moving firms and their ability to solicit prior-firm clients.
items.quote: We participate, with limited exceptions, in the Protocol for Broker Recruiting (“Protocol”), a voluntary agreement among many firms in the industry that governs, among other things, the client information that financial advisors may take with them when they affiliate with a new firm and the financial advisor’s ability to solicit clients of their prior firm.

items.text: Raymond James's value proposition is that advisors do not have to choose between culture and capabilities, offering an advisor- and client-focused culture along with leading technology, products and solutions.
items.quote: advisers do not have to choose between culture and capabilities. We offer a unique combination of an adviser and client-focused culture along with the leading technology, products and solutions advisers need to serve clients at a high level.

items.text: Raymond James recruits advisors broadly across all affiliation options rather than from any single firm or channel, and describes the pipeline as broad-based and not idiosyncratic.
items.quote: This is not a pipeline that is driven by one firm or one catalyst in the market or one affiliation option. It's a broad-based pipeline from many different -- advisers from many different firms and many different communities across the country interested in all of our -- the variety of our affiliation options.

items.text: Raymond James emphasizes consistency and a long-term approach to recruiting, rather than dialing recruiting up or down quarter-by-quarter, targeting advisors who want to stay long term rather than those moving for the highest compensation.
items.quote: it's a long-term process that requires a lot of investment, and if you dial up recruiting quarter by quarter or dial it down quarter by quarter, then you're not gonna get the quality advisors that you want. You're gonna get the advisors that are moving or not moving for the highest check, and that's not who we're targeting.

claims.text: Morgan Stanley: The firm recruits financial advisors through its advisor-led channel, while also receiving flows into that channel from its workplace funnel.

Morgan Stanley: The firm attributes advisor recruiting interest to the platform it has invested in: "There's obviously a great platform. We have recruits that are interested in what we've been investing in."

Morgan Stanley: Per a 1Q25 transcript, the firm attracts advisors by offering unique access to intellectual capital, world-class technology and compensation viewed as fair and motivating, and it is selective about recruiting.

Morgan Stanley: Per the 2Q25 10-Q (period ended June 30, 2025), the firm grants employee loans under a program established primarily to recruit certain Wealth Management financial advisors; these loans are full recourse, generally require periodic repayments, and are due in full upon termination of employment.

Merrill: Per a 4Q25 Bank of America transcript, Merrill is picking up the recruiting of experienced advisors, but this is not an enormous part of its strategy; its core approach is a training program that trains people in wealth management at Bank of America and Merrill, which the firm believes drives net new flows.

Merrill: Per a 2Q25 Bank of America transcript, Merrill adds financial advisors to the sales force in Merrill and the Private Bank through its extensive training program and experienced hiring of advisors.

Merrill: Per its web page as of 2026-11-03, the Advisor Development Program is a multi-role training path (Client Associate, Financial Solutions Advisor, Financial Advisor, Core Advisor) through which candidates obtain the SIE, Series 7 and Series 66 licenses and progress to become a Merrill Financial Advisor, with each stage lasting roughly 13 months to 1-4 years.
claims.source_label: MER press page content as of 2026-11-03 [IR]

claims.text: Merrill: Per its web page as of 2026-11-03, as part of its Advisor Development Program recruiting pitch the firm offers industry-leading training and dedicated study time to obtain securities licenses, opportunities for existing advisors with Series 7 and 66, base salary and unlimited earning potential, high-quality leads and direct client interactions, and coaching and mentorship.
claims.source_label: MER press page content as of 2026-11-03 [IR]

claims.text: Merrill: Per a November 2026 trade press report, Merrill largely pulled back from veteran broker recruiting at the end of 2017 but returned to it after Co-Presidents Lindsay Hans and Eric Schimpf (who took over in 2023) restored a focus on hiring and a more aggressive offer; recruited assets to the wealth unit doubled year-over-year as a result.

Merrill: Per a 1Q26 Bank of America transcript, the firm continues to attract talent across both new and experienced advisers, driving productivity higher on newer and existing members of the financial advisers team.

Merrill: Per a 2Q26 Bank of America transcript, Merrill and the Private Bank continue to attract talented advisers drawn to the breadth of the firm's platform and its ability to deliver comprehensive solutions for clients.

Raymond James: Per a 2Q26 transcript, the firm prefers to recruit financial advisors one-by-one rather than through acquisitions, because transition assistance fully goes to advisor retention and it lets the firm ensure cultural fit.

Raymond James: Per a 3Q26 transcript, the firm does not lead with the highest check; it seeks competitive economics but leads with culture and capabilities, offering a differentiated value proposition.
Raymond James: Per a 3Q26 transcript, the firm remains disciplined on transition assistance and the economics offered to advisors.

Raymond James: Per the fiscal 2025 10-K, the firm offers multiple affiliation options, referred to as AdvisorChoice, under which financial advisors affiliate as employees, independent contractors, or employees of third-party RIAs and broker-dealers.

Raymond James: Per the fiscal 2025 10-K, the firm participates, with limited exceptions, in the Protocol for Broker Recruiting, which governs the client information advisors may take and their ability to solicit clients when affiliating with a new firm.
Raymond James: Per the fiscal 2025 10-K, cultural fit is a requirement for both the firm's recruiting and acquisition efforts.
Raymond James: Per the 2025 investor day deck, the firm's recruiting approach includes collaborative recruiting across channels, a West Coast and Northeast focus, and a next gen advisor strategy.

Raymond James: Per a 3Q26 transcript, the firm emphasizes consistency in recruiting, noting recruiting cannot be turned on and off quarter-to-quarter and requires a consistent value proposition and a team focused on finding advisors who are good cultural fits.

Raymond James: Per trade press (September 2026), the firm builds its advisory ranks through individualized recruitment rather than large-scale acquisitions, evaluating each prospective advisor on a one-on-one basis.

Morgan Stanley: Per a 1Q25 transcript, the CEO stated people want to come onto the platform and that the firm is receiving a lot of inbound inquiry from advisors, though the firm is selective. Why it might matter: the CEO tied this to the working funnel, noting the firm added another $20 billion in the workplace product and is investing in E*TRADE and the self-directed channel.

Raymond James: Per a 2Q25 transcript, over the 12 months ended March 2025 the firm recruited into its domestic independent contractor and employee channels financial advisors with approximately $316 million of trailing 12-month production and $50 billion of client assets at their previous firms. Why it might matter: including assets recruited into its RIA and custody services division, total client assets recruited over the past 12 months were nearly $59 billion across all platforms.

Raymond James: Per a 2Q25 transcript, including assets recruited into its RIA and custody services division, the firm recruited total client assets of nearly $59 billion across all of its platforms over the past 12 months (as of March 2025). Why it might matter: quarterly domestic net new assets equaled $8.8 billion (2.6% annualized growth), a lower quarter attributed by management to factors similar to what it was seeing.

Morgan Stanley: Per a 1Q25 transcript, the CFO stated advisor recruitment remains strong, reflecting the firm's reputation as an exceptional place where financial advisors can grow their businesses. Why it might matter: in the same remarks the CFO framed advisor recruitment as part of why clients are entrusting more assets to the firm and why the business is expected to deliver durable results.

Morgan Stanley: Per a 1Q25 transcript, the firm reported strong net new assets were supported by broad-based strength across channels, including positive recruiting trends. Why it might matter: net new assets for the quarter were strong at $94 billion (6% annualized growth of beginning-period assets), so recruiting trends contributed to a strong quarter.

Raymond James: Per a 1Q25 transcript, over the prior 12 months (as of December 2024) the firm recruited financial advisors with approximately $318 million of trailing 12-month production and $51 billion of client assets to its domestic independent contractor and employee channels. Why it might matter: including assets recruited into its RIA and Custody Services (RCS) division, total client assets recruited were nearly $61 billion across all platforms, with RCS finishing the quarter up 28% year-over-year.

Raymond James: Per a 1Q25 transcript, including assets recruited into its RIA and Custody Services division, the firm recruited total client assets of nearly $61 billion across all of its platforms over the prior 12 months (as of December 2024). Why it might matter: RCS finished the quarter with $188 billion of client assets under administration, up 28% year-over-year.

The three firms' recruiting and retention approaches differ in structure and emphasis, and the reported recruiting results are not directly comparable across firms. Morgan Stanley recruits through its advisor-led channel (with flows also coming from its workplace funnel) and emphasizes its platform, intellectual capital and technology, with retention built on deferred compensation (75% cash / 25% stock) and a >99% adviser retention rate rather than retention bonuses. Merrill anchors its strategy on an internal training (Advisor Development) program while also selectively ramping veteran/experienced advisor recruiting since 2023, with retention through training, leads, mentorship and platform tools, and near-historic-low adviser attrition. Raymond James recruits one-by-one (not via acquisitions), leads with culture and AdvisorChoice multiple affiliation options rather than the highest check, and reports quantified recruiting results (trailing 12-month production and client assets). The firms' respective recruiting results differ in definition and unit: Morgan Stanley reports net new assets and qualitative recruiting strength without a separate recruiting-specific figure; Merrill reports recruited assets (doubling year-over-year) and individual team wins; Raymond James reports trailing 12-month recruited production (e.g., $538 million in fiscal 2026) and client assets. Because these use different metrics, units and periods, they are not comparable head-to-head on a single number.

a1.MS.label: different_quantity

items.text: Morgan Stanley describes the clients of its Wealth Management segment as individual investors, including high and ultra-high net worth individuals, and businesses and institutions; it does not name a 'mass-affluent' client segment.
items.quote: Wealth Management provides a comprehensive array of financial services and solutions to individual investors, including high and ultra-high net worth individuals, and businesses and institutions.

items.text: Morgan Stanley's U.S. Bank Subsidiaries and Wealth Management lending activity describe serving 'high to ultra-high net worth individuals' and 'tailored lending to ultra-high net worth clients,' rather than a mass-affluent segment.
items.quote: provide loans to a variety of customers, including large corporate and institutional clients, as well as high to ultra-high net worth individuals

items.text: The term 'mass-affluent' appears in a Morgan Stanley survey/trade publication only in reference to a third-party Cerulli Associates report about 401(k) participants, not as Morgan Stanley's own naming of a client segment.
items.quote: 52% of mass-affluent participants without an advisor say their retirement savings account provider is their primary source of retirement planning guidance.

a1.MS.differs_because: Morgan Stanley names 'high and ultra-high net worth individuals' (a higher wealth tier) as its wealth client segment, and uses 'ultra-high net worth' for its lending/institutional clients; it does not name a 'mass-affluent' segment. The only 'mass-affluent' mention is a third-party Cerulli Associates figure about 401(k) participants, not Morgan Stanley's own segment.
a1.MS.reason: Morgan Stanley does not use the term 'mass-affluent' for its own client segments; it instead names 'high and ultra-high net worth' clients, which is a different (higher) wealth segment.

a2.MS.label: different_quantity

items.text: Morgan Stanley's Wealth Management segment describes its client base as 'individual investors, including high and ultra-high net worth individuals, and businesses and institutions,' rather than mass-affluent clients.
items.quote: Wealth Management provides a comprehensive array of financial services and solutions to individual investors, including high and ultra-high net worth individuals, and businesses and institutions.

items.text: A Morgan Stanley executive described a 'more democratized offering' of alternatives to 'go to our retail client base' across the platform, referencing retail clients rather than mass-affluent clients.
items.quote: to help you provide a more democratized offering. It is certainly a focus... We think that there's great opportunity there for us and more broadly just for those alternatives across the platform to go to our retail client base.

a2.MS.differs_because: The firm describes serving 'individual investors' (specifically 'high and ultra-high net worth individuals') and 'retail' clients, but does not use the term 'mass-affluent'; these are different (wealthier or broader) client segments. The only 'mass-affluent' mention in the passages is a third-party Cerulli Associates report finding, not Morgan Stanley's own statement.
a2.MS.reason: No passage shows Morgan Stanley using the term 'mass-affluent' in its own words; it instead describes 'individual investors,' 'high and ultra-high net worth individuals,' and 'retail' clients, which are related but different client segments.

a3.MS.label: different_quantity

items.text: Ted Pick describes serving clients across all three wealth channels, including the 'everyday transaction offering' and CashPlus in E*TRADE, and the Workplace channel to 'partner with companies to reach employees.'
items.quote: We're going to service clients across all three channels in wealth: the FA channel, the everyday transaction offering, CashPlus type of offering in E*TRADE. ... we've been really banging the drum on Workplace where we can partner with companies to reach employees.

items.text: CFO Sharon Yeshaya says retail clients were engaged across the Wealth Management channels.
items.quote: Retail clients were engaged across channels.

items.text: Ted Pick refers to 20 million Wealth relationships and growth 'through the funnel' toward advisor-led assets.
items.quote: With 20 million Wealth relationships, future growth is embedded in the business. Our intense focus on the value of advice, which generates movement through the funnel, allows us to capture opportunities for advisor-led assets.

items.text: CFO Sharon Yeshaya says the firm has 20 million individual relationships across its three channels, describing a broad retail client base.
items.quote: Today, we have 20 million individual relationships across our three channels, and the opportunity to deliver incremental advice and solutions across channels and our platform remains ahead of us.

a3.MS.differs_because: Morgan Stanley describes targeting and serving a broad base of retail/individual/'everyday' clients (via E*TRADE and Workplace channels) rather than using 'mass-affluent' terminology or naming a mass-affluent segment specifically; these are wider segments that contain mass-affluent clients.
a3.MS.reason: No passage shows Morgan Stanley using 'mass-affluent' or describing a mass-affluent segment; it instead describes broad retail/individual/everyday client targeting, a wider unit containing mass-affluent clients.

a4.MS.label: not_found
a4.MS.reason: None of the passages mention 'mass-affluent' clients or specify any products, services, platforms, or fee levels offered to mass-affluent clients. The passages describe Wealth Management's general offerings (e.g., to 'individual investors,' 'high and ultra-high net worth individuals'), which is not the asked quantity specific to mass-affluent clients.

a5.MS.label: not_found
a5.MS.reason: None of the passages mention or define a mass-affluent segment in terms of asset levels or income; they cover financial results, business segments, and other metrics unrelated to a mass-affluent definition.

a6.MS.label: different_quantity

items.text: Morgan Stanley said its strategy is to introduce and educate retail clients to the value of advice, which it says sets its franchise apart and positions it to continue to outperform.
items.quote: Our intentional strategy to introduce and educate retail clients to the value of advice, coupled with consistent education over the past several years, sets our franchise apart and positions us to continue to outperform.

a6.MS.differs_because: The passage refers to 'retail clients' broadly, not specifically 'mass-affluent' clients; retail is a broader category that includes mass-affluent and other client tiers.
a6.MS.reason: No Morgan Stanley passage explicitly uses 'mass-affluent'; the closest statement concerns 'retail clients,' a broader, related segment.

claims.text: Merrill is the only firm of the five to explicitly name the mass-affluent client segment. Merrill (within Bank of America's Global Wealth & Investment Management) presents a 'Wealth Continuum' that names 'Mass Affluent ($500K - $1MM)' as a distinct client segment alongside 'High Net Worth ($1MM - $10MM)', and states it is 'Serving the wealth continuum of clients'. The comparison cannot include the other four firms on the same basis: Morgan Stanley names 'high and ultra-high net worth individuals' and 'ultra-high net worth' clients rather than a mass-affluent segment (the only 'mass-affluent' mention is a third-party Cerulli Associates report figure, not Morgan Stanley's own segment); Schwab uses 'affluent' and wealth-tier labels ('high net worth', 'ultra-high net worth', households with $1 million to $5 million) but not the specific 'mass-affluent' name; Raymond James names 'high-net-worth' and 'ultra-high-net-worth' clients (its Private Wealth Advisor program defines high-net-worth as at least $5 million in investable assets), not mass-affluent; and Edward Jones has no passage naming a mass-affluent segment.

Schwab: Wurster added that households with $1 million to $5 million in assets using only one financial services firm rose to 22%, up 11 percentage points year-over-year, which he expects to grow. Schwab: Schwab's Q2 2026 deck notes that 61% of affluent clients prefer to consolidate wealth and banking relationships. Why it might matter: the source frames this alongside the investor trend of wanting to consolidate their financial lives, which Schwab presents as an opportunity.

Merrill: In 2Q26 Merrill added ~5.4K net new $500K+ households, and Merrill and the Private Bank together added ~6K net new $500K+ relationships. Schwab: Schwab's investor day deck states that 68% of affluent investors want and are willing to pay for advice. Why it might matter: the source places this figure under Schwab's stated opportunity to grow advice market share (Schwab industry share roughly 2% of $37T), alongside a goal of increasing lending penetration.

Merrill: In 1Q26 Merrill added ~3.3K net new $500K+ households, and Merrill and the Private Bank together added ~4K net new $500K+ relationships. Why it might matter: the source lists this under Merrill Wealth Management Highlights alongside $3.8 trillion in client balances and $1.7 trillion in AUM balances for 1Q26.

Merrill: Merrill's investor-day deck presents a 'Wealth Continuum' that defines the 'Mass Affluent' segment as clients with $500K to $1MM, above which sits 'High Net Worth' ($1MM - $10MM).
