claims.text: Raymond James Financial reports financial advisor headcount as 'Total advisors,' the sum of two categories: 'Employees' (employee financial advisors) and 'Independent contractors' (independent advisors).
Raymond James Financial states that advisors in its RCS division are not included in its financial advisor metric, although their client assets are included in PCG AUA.
As of September 30, 2025, Raymond James Financial reports approximately 19,500 associates (including 3,878 employee financial advisors) and 5,065 independent advisors.

The firms define advisor headcount differently, so their figures are not compared or combined. Morgan Stanley reported 15,950 Wealth Management representatives for the quarter ended December 31, 2020, its advisor headcount figure.
Morgan Stanley reported 15,469 Wealth Management representatives for the quarter ended September 30, 2020.
Morgan Stanley reported 15,468 Wealth Management representatives for the quarter ended December 31, 2019.
The Partnership reported 20,125 financial advisors (actual) at year end 2024.
The Partnership reported 19,232 financial advisors (actual) at year end 2023.
The Partnership reported an average of 20,331 financial advisors for the year 2025, 19,650 for the year 2024, and 18,945 for the year 2023 (the source does not state the periods in a usable form).
The Partnership reported 20,429 financial advisors at period end September 26, 2025, and an average of 20,368 for the third quarter of 2025.
The Partnership reported 20,550 financial advisors at period end March 27, 2026, and an average of 20,506 for the first quarter of 2026.
The Partnership reported 20,514 financial advisors at period end June 26, 2026, and an average of 20,537 for the second quarter of 2026.
The Partnership reported 20,309 financial advisors at period end June 27, 2025, and an average of 20,316 for the second quarter of 2025.
The Partnership stated its more than 20,000 financial advisors serve more than 9 million clients as of June 26, 2026.
Bank of America reports 'Total wealth advisors' at period end of 19,130 at September 30, 2023, 19,099 at June 30, 2023, and 19,243 at March 31, 2023.
Bank of America's investor day materials report more than 15,000 wealth advisors for Merrill and Private Bank combined.

The firms define advisor headcount differently, so their figures are not compared or combined. Raymond James Financial reported 8,943 total financial advisors as of September 30, 2025, 8,787 as of September 30, 2024, and 8,712 as of September 30, 2023 (the source does not state the periods in a usable form).
Raymond James Financial reported 3,878 employee financial advisors as of September 30, 2025, 3,826 as of September 30, 2024, and 3,693 as of September 30, 2023.
Raymond James Financial reported 5,065 independent contractor financial advisors as of September 30, 2025, 4,961 as of September 30, 2024, and 5,019 as of September 30, 2023.
Raymond James Financial's advisor count comprises employee financial advisors and independent contractor financial advisors, and excludes financial advisors associated with firms in its RCS division.

claims.text: The firms define advisor headcount differently, so their figures are not compared or combined. Schwab states that growth in its headcount includes growth in financial consultants and wealth advisors, which it attributes to supporting its expanding client base.
Schwab states that higher compensation and benefits expense reflected growth in headcount, including financial consultants and wealth advisors.
Schwab describes its investor-facing advisory roles as Financial Consultants, Active Trader Financial Consultants, and Wealth Consultants, who provide guidance and relationship management.
Schwab states it is continuing to hire financial consultants and wealth advisers while expanding its branch footprint.

The firms define advisor headcount differently, so their figures are not compared or combined. Merrill (Bank of America) reports 'Total wealth advisors' at period end, which includes advisors across all wealth management businesses in GWIM and Consumer Banking; at December 31, 2023 the figure was 18,916.

The firms define advisor headcount differently, so their figures are not compared or combined. Raymond James Financial reports its financial advisor headcount as the sum of employee financial advisors and independent contractor financial advisors, shown as 'Total advisors' of 8,943 as of September 30, 2025.
Raymond James Financial's independent contractor financial advisors are called 'independent advisors' and are included in its advisor counts.

Raymond James Financial states that financial advisors associated with firms in its RCS (RIA & Custody Services) division are not included in its financial advisor counts, although their client assets are included in assets under administration (AUA).

The firms define advisor headcount differently, so their figures are not compared or combined. Morgan Stanley disclosed 'Wealth Management representatives' of 15,950 as of December 31, 2020 in its Wealth Management Metrics (Advisor-led channel), which is its financial advisor headcount metric.
Morgan Stanley disclosed 'Wealth Management representatives' of 15,469 as of September 30, 2020, and 15,468 as of December 31, 2019, in its Wealth Management Metrics.

The firms define advisor headcount differently, so their figures are not compared or combined. Schwab's filings attribute compensation and benefits expense growth to growth in headcount, including growth in financial consultants and wealth advisors, without disclosing a specific advisor headcount figure.
Schwab describes its advisor/relationship roles: Financial Consultants, Active Trader Financial Consultants, and Wealth Consultants provide guidance, relationship management, and specialized support.
Schwab's ADV Part 1A filing reports 30,690 employees, defined as including full- and part-time employees but excluding clerical workers.

Schwab's ADV Part 1A filing reports that 4,127 of its employees perform investment advisory functions (including research), and 6,584 are registered with one or more state securities authorities as investment adviser representatives.

The firms define advisor headcount differently, so their figures are not compared or combined. Edward Jones reports financial advisor headcount under the metric label 'Financial advisors (actual),' disclosing both the count at period end and the average for the period; at year end 2025 the Partnership reported 20,425 financial advisors.
The Partnership also reports the average number of financial advisors for the period; the average for 2025 was 20,331.
The Partnership reports financial advisor headcount by geographic segment; at year end 2025 the U.S. segment had 19,540 financial advisors and the Canada segment had 885.

The Partnership discloses financial advisor headcount as 'Financial advisors (actual),' reported 'At period end' and 'Average' and split between U.S. and Canada segments; the parenthetical '(actual)' indicates advisors are counted as actual individuals rather than on a full-time equivalent basis.

The firms define advisor headcount differently, so their figures are not compared or combined. Bank of America's Global Wealth & Investment Management Key Indicators report advisor headcount as 'Total wealth advisors' at period end, a metric defined as including advisors across all wealth management businesses in GWIM and Consumer Banking.
Total wealth advisors at period end were 18,916 at December 31, 2023, and 19,273 at December 31, 2022.
The 2025 Investor Day deck describes Merrill and the Private Bank as having an industry-leading advisor force of wealth advisors.

The firms define advisor headcount differently, so their figures are not compared or combined. Raymond James Financial reports advisor headcount as 'Financial advisors,' broken into 'Employees' (employee financial advisors) and 'Independent contractors,' with a 'Total advisors' line, as of each September 30.
As of September 30, 2025, Raymond James Financial reported 3,878 employee financial advisors and 5,065 independent contractor advisors.

Raymond James Financial states that advisors in its RCS (RIA & Custody Services) division are not included in its financial advisor metric, although their client assets are included in PCG AUA; financial advisors associated with firms in the RCS division are not included in its financial advisor counts, although their client assets are included in AUA.

a1.SCHW.label: fact

items.text: Schwab states that as one of the largest investment services firms in the U.S., its scale lets it spread operating costs and amortize new investments over a large base of clients.
items.quote: As one of the largest investment services firms in the U.S., we are able to spread operating costs and amortize new investments over a large base of clients, and harness the resources to evolve capabilities to meet client needs.

items.text: Schwab states that its operating efficiency, coupled with scale and sharing of infrastructure across businesses, creates a cost advantage enabling competitive pricing while profitably serving clients across channels.
items.quote: Coupled with scale, our operating efficiency and sharing of infrastructure across different businesses creates a cost advantage that enables us to competitively price products and services while profitably serving clients of various sizes across multiple channels.

items.text: Schwab states that its sheer scale combined with efficiency efforts keeps its cost-to-serve clients low, which allows it to invest in client capabilities that fuel growth.
items.quote: our sheer scale, combined with efficiency efforts that make it easier for clients to do business with us, keeps our cost-to-serve clients low. This also allows us to invest in client capabilities that will fuel our growth

items.text: Schwab states that its scale combined with expense discipline decreased its cost per account 20% over the last five years, driving industry leadership in expense on client assets (EOCA).
items.quote: Our scale, combined with our expense discipline, has allowed us to decrease our cost per account 20% over the last five years while driving our ability to remain the industry leader as measured by expense on client assets, or EOCA

items.text: Schwab states it improved cost per account by more than 20% over the last decade.
items.quote: This balanced approach to expense management has enabled us to drive expense on client assets down into the low double digits and improve cost per account by more than 20% over the last decade.

items.text: Schwab states that its marketing spend drives approximately 40% of new-to-firm retail clients.
items.quote: We are investing in our marketing spend, which drives approximately 40% of new-to-firm retail clients.

items.text: Schwab states that its marketing uses a data and insight-led model that drives efficiency at scale.
items.quote: Our data & insight-led model drives efficiency at scale

items.text: Schwab states that 90% of accounts are opened digitally and that it leverages its scale to maintain a structural cost advantage while continuing to invest in growth.
items.quote: 90% Accounts opened digitally ... Leverage our scale to maintain a structural cost advantage while continuing to invest in growth

items.text: Schwab states that its marketing team is using answer engine optimization to ensure it shows up on the AI platforms where investors search, to reach more prospects and clients.
items.quote: We're already reaching a growing number of clients through the answer engine optimization work that our marketing team is doing to ensure we show up on the AI platforms where investors return.

items.text: Schwab states its scale and efficiency efforts drive productivity, keep its structural cost advantage, and allow it to reinvest in new capabilities and growth.
items.quote: We have several goals with our scale and efficiency efforts to drive productivity, make Schwab easier to work with and keep our structural cost advantage, all of which allow us to reinvest in new capabilities and growth.

items.text: Schwab states that its broader set of capabilities spanning wealth management, trading, banking, and asset management helps it efficiently attract a wide range of investors, driving sustainable organic growth, and that its scale and efficiency is a significant competitive advantage enabling it to maintain key investments.
items.quote: The broader set of capabilities, which spans wealth management, trading, banking, asset management, and much more, helps us efficiently attract a wide range of investors driving sustainable organic growth and allows us to deepen relationships with our clients as their needs change over time... our scale and efficiency is a significant competitive advantage, enabling us to maintain key investments and flexibility to navigate various macroeconomic environments.

items.text: Schwab keeps costs low and reinvests in new capabilities to make it easier for clients to work with the firm.
items.quote: to make it easier for clients to work with us while keeping costs low & reinvesting in new capabilities

items.text: Schwab is attracting net new assets and new clients while investing in scale and efficiency initiatives.
items.quote: We're attracting net new assets and new clients to Schwab as we deepen relationships to serve even more of their wealth and financial needs. We're investing in scale and efficiency initiatives

items.text: Traders come to Schwab for its platforms, capabilities, education, coaching, and service, and in 2025 about half of new-to-firm retail clients initiated access to Schwab's thinkorswim platform.
items.quote: Traders come to Schwab because we provide the platforms, capabilities, education, coaching, and service they need... In 2025, about half of new-to-firm retail clients initiated access to our industry-leading thinkorswim platform.

a1.SCHW.reason: The passages directly describe the mechanisms by which Schwab uses its scale (spreading costs, low cost-to-serve, marketing efficiency, digital account opening) to acquire clients cheaply.

a5.EDJ.label: fact

items.text: Edward Jones targets new clients through initiatives including High Net Worth (attracting and serving high net worth clients through expanded advice, planning, products and services across multiple service models), Workplace (connecting local business owners and their employees with financial solutions through their workplace), and a new digital platform focused on attracting and retaining Next Generation investors.
items.quote: These initiatives also include targeting new clients: High Net Worth, focused on attracting and serving high net worth clients through expanded advice, planning, products and services across multiple service models; Workplace, which connects local business owners and their employees with financial solutions through their workplace; and a new digital platform, focused on attracting and retaining Next Generation investors.

items.text: Edward Jones acquires and serves clients through its branch office model, in which financial advisors and client support team professionals located in the communities where clients live and work build deep, personal relationships and provide comprehensive advice and planning.
items.quote: The Partnership's branch office model is designed to serve clients through deep, personal relationships and comprehensive advice and planning with financial advisors and client support team professionals ("CSTPs") located in the communities where clients live and work.

items.text: Edward Jones advisors work with local business owners every day, leveraging the firm's footprint in local communities to prospect and win workplace retirement plans through a new end-to-end retirement plan management technology platform covering the full plan lifecycle from prospecting to plan servicing.
items.quote: Given our strong footprint in our communities, our advisors are working with local business owners every single day... RPMC will leverage Aboon Workplace, an AI-native platform that lets advisors find and win retirement plans all in one place.

a5.EDJ.reason: The passages describe Edward Jones' client acquisition approaches: targeted initiatives (High Net Worth, Workplace, digital/Next Generation platform) and a community-based branch model plus workplace retirement-plan prospecting.

a6.EDJ.label: fact

items.text: Edward Jones's operating expenses increased 11% to $15,610 million in 2025, primarily due to increases in compensation and benefits expense, variable compensation, and communications and data processing expense.
items.quote: Operating expenses increased 11% to $15,610 in 2025, primarily due to increases in compensation and benefits expense, variable compensation and communications and data processing expense.

items.text: Edward Jones's income before allocations was $2,090 million in 2025, and income before allocations margin was 11.7%, which the firm describes as reflecting a strategic balance between investing in the future and current financial results.
items.quote: the increase in net revenue, partially offset by the increase in operating expenses, generated income before allocations of $2,090, a 6% increase from 2024. Income before allocations margin was 11.7%, reflecting a strategic balance between investing in the future and current financial results.

items.text: Edward Jones's financial advisor compensation and benefits expense increased 12% to $6,969 million in 2025, primarily due to increases in revenues on which commissions are earned.
items.quote: Financial advisor compensation and benefits expense increased 12% to $6,969 in 2025. The increase was primarily due to increases in revenues on which commissions are earned.

items.text: Edward Jones's variable compensation increased 11% to $2,710 million in 2025, which the firm describes as expanding and contracting in relation to the Partnership's profitability and margin earned, and as a key component of its performance-based compensation model.
items.quote: The increase in variable compensation of 11% to $2,710 in 2025 was primarily due to increased branch and overall Firm profitability.

items.text: Edward Jones's communications and data processing expense increased 16% to $1,162 million in 2025, primarily due to continued investments in new tools and technology and higher depreciation expense from recent investments.
items.quote: Communications and data processing expense increased 16% to $1,162 in 2025 primarily due to continued investments in new tools and technology and higher depreciation expense as a result of these recent investments.

items.quote: Advertising                                                            43                              39

items.quote: These initiatives also include targeting new clients: High Net Worth, focused on attracting and serving high net worth clients through expanded advice, planning, products and services across multiple service models; Workplace, which connects local business owners and their employees with financial solutions through their workplace; and a new digital platform, focused on attracting and retaining Next Generation investors.

items.text: Edward Jones has partnered with Aboon (an AI-driven third-party administrator) and Retirement Plan Advisory Group to develop an end-to-end retirement plan management tool to help its advisors better serve business owners and their employees, as part of its workplace retirement efforts.

The firm hopes the new technology will help its advisors better serve business owners and their employees.

a7.EDJ.label: fact

items.text: Edward Jones's existing client-serving model is its branch office network, which the firm describes as designed to serve clients through deep, personal relationships and comprehensive advice and planning with financial advisors and client support team professionals located in the communities where clients live and work.
items.quote: The Partnership's branch office model is designed to serve clients through deep, personal relationships and comprehensive advice and planning with financial advisors and client support team professionals ("CSTPs") located in the communities where clients live and work.

items.text: Edward Jones's stated strategic ambition includes continuing to invest in technology to scale its ability to provide financial planning to clients, and to attract and serve new client segments.
items.quote: Continue investing in technology to scale our ability to provide financial planning to our clients • Anticipate clients' needs with the right offering at the right time, now and for generations to come • Attract and serve new client segments

items.text: Edward Jones's initiatives for targeting new clients include High Net Worth (attracting and serving high net worth clients through expanded advice, planning, products and services across multiple service models), Workplace (connecting local business owners and their employees with financial solutions through their workplace), and a new digital platform focused on attracting and retaining Next Generation investors.
items.quote: These initiatives also include targeting new clients: High Net Worth, focused on attracting and serving high net worth clients through expanded advice, planning, products and services across multiple service models; Workplace, which connects local business owners and their employees with financial solutions through their workplace; and a new digital platform, focused on attracting and retaining Next Generation investors.

items.text: Edward Jones announced it has taken a minority stake in the personal finance app Quicken, with the stated intention that the investment is a step towards integrating Quicken's personal financial management capabilities more directly into Edward Jones to support its value proposition and advisor conversations with clients; the firm notes it is still determining the actual deployment strategy for how Quicken will be offered to clients and integrated into its internal advisor software platforms.
items.quote: Edward Jones announced that they have taken a minority stake in the personal finance app Quicken, with an explicit intention that the investment is a step towards integrating Quicken's personal financial management capabilities more directly into Edward Jones as a way to support their value proposition and advisor conversations with clients.

items.text: Edward Jones is integrating a technology platform (RPMC, leveraging Aboon Workplace) into its advisor workstation that will cover the entire workplace retirement plan lifecycle, from prospecting to plan servicing, with a prospecting module currently in beta and expected to go live to the broader network early next year.

a1.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley describes its three channels—financial advisors, Workplace, and E*TRADE—as comprising its 'strategic client acquisition model,' positioning Workplace as the top of the funnel for acquiring wealth management clients.
items.quote: Our financial advisors, Workplace, and E*TRADE, each a category leader, which taken together comprise our strategic client acquisition model.

items.text: The CFO describes the funnel as beginning with retaining vested workplace assets (which translates into net new assets), followed over time by channel migration where workplace assets 'seek advice' and move into the adviser-led channel.
items.quote: The first is we retain those assets, and we'll see -- in this particular quarter, we saw greater asset retention from Workplace, which translated into NNA. And then over time ... we are seeing channel migration, and that's with technology and investment, where those Workplace assets are now actually seeking advice and that migration is something that has helped to contribute to over $1 trillion of total assets in our adviser-led strategy.

items.text: Morgan Stanley describes 'channel migration' as workplace assets that began in the Workplace channel moving into the advisor-led channel, with $300 billion doing so since 2020.
items.quote: what I mean by channel migration is we have Workplace assets that began at some point in Workplace, and we're seeing them move into the advisor-led concept. Over the last five years or so, since 2020, we've seen $300 billion coming and initiating at some point from Workplace and moving into that advisor-led channel.

items.text: Morgan Stanley attributes the migration of workplace-originated assets into the advisor-led channel to its consistent investments in its differentiated platform.
items.quote: Assets that originated from workplace continue to migrate into our advisor-led channel as a result of the consistent investments we have made into our differentiated platform.

items.text: Morgan Stanley describes Workplace as bringing relationships and assets onto the platform, and then delivering advice and solutions to those relationships to build fee-based assets.
items.quote: Workplace brings relationships and assets onto the platform, and we are well positioned to support these new relationships. ... We continue to deliver advice and solutions to new and existing relationships, supporting the build in our fee-based assets.

items.text: Morgan Stanley describes its Morgan Stanley at Work business as positioning it as an early trusted advisor to private companies, where employees benefit from management of equity compensation plans, liquidity opportunities, and full-service advice as companies grow.
items.quote: Our Morgan Stanley at Work business, with its exclusive partnership with Carta, positions us as an early trusted advisor to over 50,000 private companies. As workplace companies grow, we can provide traditional institutional servicing. Employees across our workplace companies benefit from our management of equity compensation plans, liquidity opportunities, and our full-service advice.

items.text: Morgan Stanley describes its investments in the self-directed and Workplace channels as driving its 'differentiated client acquisition funnel.'
items.quote: In Wealth Management, investments in our self-directed and Workplace channels drive our differentiated client acquisition funnel.

items.text: Morgan Stanley states that 70% of the flows originating from workplace are net new assets to the firm.
items.quote: 70% of the flows that come from workplace, that originate from workplace, is actually net new assets to the firm.

items.text: Morgan Stanley states that since 2020 it has generated over $400 billion of new adviser-led assets from relationships that originated from either Workplace or E*TRADE.
items.quote: Since 2020, we have generated over $400 billion of new adviser-led assets from relationships that originated from either Workplace or E*TRADE.

items.text: Morgan Stanley describes a referral-based partnership with Carta under which private companies moving from private to public are referred to Morgan Stanley, supporting conversion into its platform.
items.quote: The original relationship started as a referral-based model. As companies began to move from a private side to a public side, they would be referred to Morgan Stanley.

items.text: Morgan Stanley's strategic-update deck depicts a client lifecycle in which workplace founders and employees move from financial wellness and equity compensation through to 'Full-Service Wealth Advice and Asset Allocation' as companies go public.
items.quote: Financial Wellness and Employee Benefits ... Full-Service Wealth Advice and Asset Allocation ... IPO Execution and Support Services

a1.MS.reason: The passages contain multiple explicit statements from executives describing how the firm converts workplace participants into wealth management clients through its client acquisition funnel and channel migration.

items.text: Morgan Stanley defines stock plan participants as total accounts with vested and/or unvested stock plan assets in the workplace channel, with individuals holding accounts in multiple plans counted in each plan.
items.quote: Stock plan participants represent total accounts with vested and/or unvested stock plan assets in the workplace channel. Individuals with accounts in multiple plans are counted as participants in each plan.
items.definition: total accounts with vested and/or unvested stock plan assets in the workplace channel

a1.RJF.label: fact

items.text: Raymond James refers to its multiple affiliation options as AdvisorChoice®, under which financial advisors affiliate directly as either employees or independent contractors, or as employees of third-party Registered Investment Advisors and broker-dealers serviced through the RIA and Custody Services division.
items.quote: We offer multiple affiliation options, which we refer to as AdvisorChoice®. Financial advisors primarily affiliate with us directly as either employees or independent contractors or as employees of third-party Registered Investment Advisors (“RIAs”) and broker-dealers to which we provide services through our RIA and Custody Services (“RCS”) division.

items.text: AdvisorChoice® is described as a platform of dynamic options and the freedom to choose among them, letting advisors match their professional goals to the affiliation option that is right for them.
items.quote: Through AdvisorChoice®, you have the ability to match your professional goals to the affiliation option that’s right for you, each offering a unique combination of support, freedom and flexibility... AdvisorChoice® A platform of dynamic options and the freedom to choose among them.

items.text: The affiliation options listed by Raymond James include Traditional Employee, Advisor Select, Independent Contractor, Bank & Credit Union, and Corporate RIA.
items.quote: Traditional Employee: Get everything you expect from working for a firm with a powerful difference – book ownership. Advisor Select: Lead your own branch with access to administrative support and full corporate benefits. Independent Contractor: Operate as an independent financial advisor backed by the resources of a national leader. Bank & Credit Union: Leverage national strength and local impact to grow your advisory business. Corporate RIA: Exercise true autonomy and support refined for fee-only practices under our established RIA.

items.text: Employee financial advisors work in a traditional branch supported by local management and administrative staff, serve predominantly retail clients, and are compensated primarily through a payout on the revenues they generate, also participating in the firm's employee benefit plans.
items.quote: Employee financial advisors work in a traditional branch supported by local management and administrative staff. They provide services predominantly to retail clients. Compensation for these financial advisors primarily includes a payout on revenues they generate and such advisors also participate in the firm’s employee benefit plans.

items.text: Under the Traditional Employee model, advisors receive up to a 50% payout plus a full array of competitive employee benefits, with minimum 5 years of experience required.
items.quote: Model: Traditional Employee Qualifications*: Minimum 5 years of experience and production qualifications vary. Payout + Benefits: Up to 50% payout** and full array of competitive employee benefits offerings.

items.text: Under the Advisor Select model, advisors receive a 70-80% gross payout plus a full array of competitive employee benefits, and run their own branch (an employee affiliation option for advisors who want to lead a team).
items.quote: Model: Advisor Select Qualifications*: Minimum 3 years of experience and $3.5 million or higher in annual branch fees and commission revenue. Payout + Benefits: 70-80% gross payout** and full array of competitive employee benefits offerings.

items.text: Under the Independent Contractor model, advisors receive an 81% to 90% payout, and leverage Raymond James' third-party partnerships to build their own benefits package.
items.quote: Model: Independent Contractor Qualifications*: Minimum 3 years of experience. Minimum T12 of $150,000 required to join an existing branch and $400,000 to open a new branch. Payout + Benefits: 81% to 90% payout***. Leverage our third party partnerships to create a benefits package that best fits your team.

items.text: Independent contractor financial advisors are generally responsible for all of their direct costs and, accordingly, receive a higher payout percentage on the revenues they generate than employee financial advisors.
items.quote: Our financial advisors who are independent contractors are generally responsible for all of their direct costs and, accordingly, receive a higher payout percentage on the revenues they generate than employee financial advisors.

items.text: Independent payouts are higher than employee payouts because independent advisors cover their own overhead costs, real estate, health insurance, etc.; the employee side uses tiered payout systems where higher production moves an advisor up the payout grid.
items.quote: with the compensation and payouts to independent advisers versus employee advisers, of course, the independent payouts are higher because they cover their overhead costs, their real estate, their health insurance, et cetera... even on the employee side, we have tiered payout systems. And so as production increases, you kind of get higher up on the payout grid as well.

items.text: Independent contractor financial advisors may affiliate directly or through an affiliated bank or credit union in the Financial Institutions Division, and with specific approval may conduct certain other approved business activities such as insurance products, independent RIA services, and accounting and tax services.
items.quote: Independent contractor financial advisors may affiliate with us directly or through an affiliated bank or credit union in our Financial Institutions Division. With specific approval, and on a limited basis, they are permitted to conduct certain other approved business activities, such as offering insurance products, independent registered investment advisory services, and accounting and tax services.

items.text: Raymond James states it is agnostic about how an advisor affiliates (employee vs independent contractor vs RIA custody), wanting advisors to choose based on fit with its culture, values, platform and capabilities.
items.quote: we have adviser choice where we're agnostic into how you affiliate with Raymond James. We want you to fall in love with our culture, values and the platform and capabilities and how you affiliate with us, we're indifferent to.

items.text: The affiliation spectrum ranges from employee (RJA) to independent contractor (ICD) to RIA & Custody Services, described by Raymond James as servicing the largest addressable market in the industry.
items.quote: EMPLOYEE INDEPENDENT CONTRACTOR RIA & CUSTODY SERVICES EMPLOYEE ADVISOR (RJA) ADVISOR SELECT INDEPENDENT ADVISOR (ICD) BANKS AND CREDIT UNIONS IAR* (CORPORATE RIA) RIA** & CUSTODY SERVICES The movement to "independence" is not channel-specific

items.text: Management states Raymond James does not lead with the highest transition check but leads with culture and capabilities, requiring competitive economics while offering a differentiated value proposition, and remaining disciplined on transition assistance and advisor economics.
items.quote: we don't lead with the highest check. We want to have competitive economics. Certainly, we have to have competitive economics, but we lead with culture and capabilities. And so we have a true differentiated value proposition.

items.text: Management states the firm is focused on the long term and providing a stable platform, attracting and retaining advisors with unique culture, leading service and robust platform rather than the largest check.
items.quote: We are focused on the long-term and providing a stable platform for our advisors, bankers, and associates... We attract and retain financial advisors with our unique culture, leading service, and robust platform, whereas many of our competitors compete with the largest check.

items.text: Management states Raymond James values independence to foster an environment where advisors can provide objective advice, unlike competitors that change comp plans each year to cross-sell bank products.
items.quote: We value independence to foster an environment where our advisors can provide objective advice to their clients, whereas many of our competitors change their comp plans every year to cross-sell more bank products.

items.text: Management states the firm has the largest addressable market in the industry because it offers all affiliation options and is agnostic about how advisors affiliate, wanting them drawn to its culture, values, platform and capabilities.
items.quote: we have the largest addressable market in the industry because we have all the affiliation options that an adviser could possibly want. And we have adviser choice where we're agnostic into how you affiliate with Raymond James.

items.text: Management states advisors do not have to choose between culture and capabilities, offering a unique combination of an advisor- and client-focused culture with leading technology, products and solutions.
items.quote: advisers do not have to choose between culture and capabilities. We offer a unique combination of an adviser and client-focused culture together with leading technologies, products and solutions advisers need to serve clients at a high level.

items.text: Management states the firm has the largest addressable market across its affiliation options (employee to independent contractor to RIA custody) with critical mass and decades of experience in all of them.
items.quote: we have the largest addressable market across our affiliation options, from employee to independent contractor to the RIA custody, and we have critical mass and decades of experience in all of them.

items.text: Management describes advisor recruiting as a long-term 'marathon, not a sprint,' targeting advisors who want to stay long-term rather than those moving for the highest check.
items.quote: We have to have a competitive check, but we want the advisors that want to be here over the long term to make more money and be satisfied here over the rest of their careers.

items.text: Management states consistency is a critical concept in recruiting and retaining advisors, focusing on finding advisors who are good cultural fits across affiliation options.
items.quote: you have to be consistent in that value proposition that I described and retaining your existing advisers, recruiting new advisers, having the team focused on finding advisers that are good cultural fits with the firm across our affiliation options. Consistency is a critical sort of concept for us, not only in recruiting, but across the results that we generate.

items.text: Management describes a 'best of both worlds' value proposition combining scope and breadth of products and capabilities with a culture anchored on putting people first.
items.quote: We are unique in having the scope and breadth of products and capabilities to serve complex needs of clients, combined with our strong culture that is anchored on putting people first.

items.text: Management states its strong balance sheet and commitment to independence are proving to be a differentiator for advisors evaluating alternatives.
items.quote: our strong balance sheet and commitment to independence is proving to be a differentiator for advisors evaluating alternatives.

items.text: Management (per trade press) states the advisor, not the home office, is the client, and that the firm builds its advisory ranks through individualized recruitment rather than large-scale acquisitions, evaluating each prospective advisor one-on-one.
items.quote: both Chief Executive Officer Paul Shoukry and Elwyn said the advisor, not the home office, is the client - and framed every platform enhancement as a function of that philosophy... Shoukry has emphasized the firm's strategy of building its advisory ranks through individualized recruitment rather than large-scale acquisitions, noting that the firm evaluates each prospective advisor on a one-on-one basis.

a5.RJF.reason: Multiple passages contain management's stated strategic rationale and priorities for the affiliation-choice model (culture and capabilities over price, long-term focus, independence, largest addressable market, agnostic affiliation, advisor-as-client).

claims.text: Raymond James Financial: Raymond James refers to its multiple affiliation options as AdvisorChoice®, under which financial advisors affiliate directly as either employees or independent contractors, or as employees of third-party RIAs and broker-dealers serviced through the RIA and Custody Services division (FY2025).

Raymond James Financial: The affiliation options listed by Raymond James include Traditional Employee, Advisor Select, Independent Contractor, Bank & Credit Union, and Corporate RIA (page content as of 2026-04-21).
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]

claims.text: Raymond James Financial: Employee financial advisors work in a traditional branch supported by local management and administrative staff, serve predominantly retail clients, and are compensated primarily through a payout on the revenues they generate, also participating in the firm's employee benefit plans (FY2025).

Raymond James Financial: Under the Traditional Employee model, advisors receive up to a 50% payout plus a full array of competitive employee benefits, with minimum 5 years of experience required (page content as of 2026-04-21).
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]

claims.text: Raymond James Financial: Under the Advisor Select model, advisors receive a 70-80% gross payout plus a full array of competitive employee benefits, and run their own branch (an employee affiliation option for advisors who want to lead a team) (page content as of 2026-04-21).
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]

claims.text: Raymond James Financial: Under the Independent Contractor model, advisors receive an 81% to 90% payout, and leverage Raymond James' third-party partnerships to build their own benefits package (page content as of 2026-04-21).
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]

claims.text: Raymond James Financial: Independent contractor financial advisors are generally responsible for all of their direct costs and, accordingly, receive a higher payout percentage on the revenues they generate than employee financial advisors (FY2025).

Raymond James Financial: On the 3Q26 earnings call (period ended March 31, 2026), management said independent payouts are higher than employee payouts because independent advisors cover their own overhead costs, real estate, health insurance, etc.; the employee side uses tiered payout systems where higher production moves an advisor up the payout grid.

Raymond James Financial: Independent contractor financial advisors may affiliate directly or through an affiliated bank or credit union in the Financial Institutions Division, and with specific approval may conduct certain other approved business activities such as insurance products, independent RIA services, and accounting and tax services (FY2025).

Raymond James Financial: On the 4Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), management said Raymond James is agnostic about how an advisor affiliates (employee vs independent contractor vs RIA custody), wanting advisors to choose based on fit with its culture, values, platform and capabilities.

Raymond James Financial: The affiliation spectrum ranges from employee (RJA) to independent contractor (ICD) to RIA & Custody Services, described by Raymond James as servicing the largest addressable market in the industry (Investor Day deck, June 2025).

Raymond James Financial: How the affiliation-choice model works commercially (payouts, fees, economics by affiliation type): Under the Bank & Credit Union model, advisors receive a competitive compensation package from the financial institution in partnership with Raymond James (page content as of 2026-04-21).
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]

claims.text: Raymond James Financial: Under the Corporate RIA model, advisors receive an 81% to 90% payout and build their own benefits package through third-party partnerships (page content as of 2026-04-21).
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]

claims.text: Raymond James Financial: Under the RIA & Custody Services model, advisors work with their RIA or broker/dealer to determine compensation and create their own benefits package (page content as of 2026-04-21).
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]

claims.text: Raymond James Financial: On the 4Q24 earnings call (period ended September 30, 2024), management said that for RIA custody, the margin on a P&L basis is actually higher because the attachment revenue booked is much lower, whereas in other businesses Raymond James grosses up the revenues pre-payout; ROCA varies with the RIA's asset mix and pricing structure.
Raymond James Financial: For firms affiliated through the RIA and Custody Services division, revenues related to their assets in the PCG segment are included in Account and service fees (FY2025).
Raymond James Financial: As of September 30, 2025, Raymond James reported 8,943 total financial advisors, consisting of 3,878 employee financial advisors and 5,065 independent contractor advisors.
Raymond James Financial: As of September 30, 2024, Raymond James reported 8,787 total financial advisors, consisting of 3,826 employees and 4,961 independent contractors.
Raymond James Financial: As of September 30, 2023, Raymond James reported 8,712 total financial advisors, consisting of 3,693 employees and 5,019 independent contractors.

Raymond James Financial: On the fiscal 4Q25 earnings call (October 2025), management said Raymond James ended fiscal 2025 with a record number of financial advisors, 2% higher than the prior year, reflecting solid advisor retention and strong recruiting results.

Raymond James Financial: For fiscal 2025 (domestic independent contractor and employee channels), Raymond James reported record trailing 12-month production for recruited financial advisors of $407 million.

Raymond James Financial: Through the first 9 months of fiscal 2026, Raymond James recruited advisors with trailing 12-month production totaling $393 million (domestic independent contractor and employee channels).

Raymond James Financial: In the fiscal third quarter (period ended June 30, 2026), Raymond James recruited financial advisors to its domestic independent contractor and employee channels with trailing 12-month production totaling $156 million.

Raymond James Financial: In the fiscal second quarter (period ended March 31, 2026), Raymond James recruited financial advisors to its domestic independent contractor and employee channels with trailing 12-month production totaling $141 million, the second-highest quarterly result in its history.
Raymond James Financial: For the year ended September 30, 2025, Raymond James's domestic financial advisor retention remained very strong.

Raymond James Financial: On the 4Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), CEO Paul Shoukry said Raymond James reports a 97% advisor satisfaction rate with its surveys, which he described as the best he knows of in the industry, and cited this retention as the foundation for growth.

Raymond James Financial: Raymond James defines domestic Private Client Group net new assets as domestic Private Client Group client inflows, including dividends and interest, less domestic Private Client Group client outflows, including commissions, advisory fees, and other fees.

Raymond James Financial: On the 4Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), management stated Raymond James does not lead with the highest transition check but leads with culture and capabilities, requiring competitive economics while offering a differentiated value proposition, and remaining disciplined on transition assistance and advisor economics.

Raymond James Financial: On the fiscal 4Q25 earnings call (October 2025), management stated the firm is focused on the long term and providing a stable platform, attracting and retaining advisors with unique culture, leading service and robust platform rather than the largest check.

Raymond James Financial: On the fiscal 4Q25 earnings call (October 2025), management stated Raymond James values independence to foster an environment where advisors can provide objective advice, unlike competitors that change comp plans each year to cross-sell bank products.

Raymond James Financial: On the 4Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), management stated the firm has the largest addressable market in the industry because it offers all affiliation options and is agnostic about how advisors affiliate, wanting them drawn to its culture, values, platform and capabilities.

Raymond James Financial: On the 2Q26 earnings call (period ended March 31, 2026), management stated advisors do not have to choose between culture and capabilities, offering a unique combination of an advisor- and client-focused culture with leading technology, products and solutions.

Raymond James Financial: On the 1Q26 earnings call (period ended December 31, 2025), management stated the firm has the largest addressable market across its affiliation options (employee to independent contractor to RIA custody) with critical mass and decades of experience in all of them.

Raymond James Financial: On the 1Q26 earnings call (period ended December 31, 2025), management described advisor recruiting as a long-term marathon, not a sprint, targeting advisors who want to stay long-term rather than those moving for the highest check.

Raymond James Financial: On the 4Q26 earnings call (period ended June 30, 2026), management stated consistency is a critical concept in recruiting and retaining advisors, focusing on finding advisors who are good cultural fits across affiliation options.

Raymond James Financial: On the 1Q25 earnings call (period ended December 31, 2024), management described a 'best of both worlds' value proposition combining scope and breadth of products and capabilities with a culture anchored on putting people first.

Raymond James Financial: On the fiscal 4Q25 earnings call (October 2025), management stated its strong balance sheet and commitment to independence is proving to be a differentiator for advisors evaluating alternatives.

Raymond James Financial: Trade press reports that management stated the advisor, not the home office, is the client, and that the firm builds its advisory ranks through individualized recruitment rather than large-scale acquisitions, evaluating each prospective advisor one-on-one (published September 2026).

items.text: Raymond James's Private Client Group segment earns revenue by charging either asset-based fees (recorded as 'Asset management and related administrative fees') or sales commissions (recorded as 'Brokerage revenues') for the financial planning, investment advisory, and securities transaction services it provides.
items.quote: Through our PCG segment, we provide financial planning, investment advisory, and securities transaction services for which we generally charge either asset-based fees (presented in "Asset management and related administrative fees") or sales commissions (presented in "Brokerage revenues").

items.text: Raymond James earns asset management and related administrative fees for performing asset management, portfolio management, and related investment services for retail clients for assets invested in fee-based accounts, and earns commissions and distribution-related revenues for brokerage accounts.
items.quote: We earn asset management and related administrative fees in this segment for performing asset management, portfolio management, and related investment services for retail clients for assets invested in fee-based accounts. ... We also earn commissions for executing and clearing transactions for clients, primarily in listed and over-the-counter equity securities, including exchange-traded funds ("ETFs"), options, and fixed income products.

items.text: The PCG segment also earns servicing fee revenues from third-party mutual fund and annuity companies whose products it distributes and from banks to which it sweeps client cash deposits (RJBDP), and earns net interest on assets segregated for regulatory purposes, margin loans, cash balances, and securities borrowing transactions.
items.quote: The segment includes servicing fee revenues from third-party mutual fund and annuity companies whose products we distribute and from banks to which we sweep a portion of our clients' cash deposits as part of the RJBDP, our multi-bank sweep program. The segment also includes net interest earnings primarily on assets segregated for regulatory purposes, margin loans provided to clients, cash balances, and securities borrowing transactions...

items.text: Revenues related to fee-based accounts under administration in PCG are shared between the PCG and Asset Management segments, with the Asset Management segment receiving a higher portion for accounts in managed programs because it performs portfolio management in addition to administrative services.
items.quote: Revenues related to fee-based accounts under administration in PCG are shared by the PCG and Asset Management segments, the amount of which depends on whether clients are invested in "managed programs"... The Asset Management segment receives a higher portion of the revenues related to accounts invested in managed programs, as compared to the portion received for non-managed programs, as it is performing portfolio management services in addition to administrative services.
items.scope: Private Client Group and Asset Management segments

claims.text: Schwab: Schwab states that its largest sources of net revenues are net interest revenue, asset management and administration fees, trading revenue, and bank deposit account fees, supported by the combination of its broker-dealer, bank, and asset management operating subsidiaries.

Schwab: Schwab states that asset management and administration fees are primarily earned from proprietary money market mutual funds, proprietary and third-party mutual funds and ETFs, and fee-based managed investing solutions.

Schwab: Schwab states that trading revenue includes commissions earned for executing trades for clients in certain individual equities, options, futures, fixed income securities, and certain third-party mutual funds and ETFs; order flow revenue; and principal transactions revenue earned primarily from actions to support client trading in fixed income securities.

Schwab: The 10-K (period 2025-12-31) states Schwab earns bank deposit account fee revenue from the TD Depository Institutions under the 2023 IDA agreement, presented net of interest paid to clients and other applicable fees.

Morgan Stanley: Within the Wealth Management business segment, asset management revenues are related to advisory services associated with fee-based assets, account service and administration, and distribution of products, and are generally based on the net asset value of the account in which a client is invested.
Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley defines fee-based client assets as the amount of client assets where the basis of payment for services is a fee calculated on those assets.

Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley reports an average fee rate of 78 basis points on Advisor fee-based accounts for 2025, with the overall total fee-based client assets average fee rate of 63 basis points, based on asset management revenues related to advisory services associated with fee-based assets.

Edward Jones: Edward Jones states that its asset-based fees include advisory program fees, which are based on the average daily market value of client assets in the program, as well as contractual rates.

Edward Jones: The primary source of the firm's asset-based fee revenue is program fees for investment advisory services, with revenue derived from fees determined by the underlying value of client assets.
Edward Jones: The firm earns revenue on clients' assets through service fees and revenue sharing received under agreements with certain mutual fund and insurance companies.
Edward Jones: Cash solutions revenue is earned from the Edward Jones Insured Bank Deposit Program, an interest-bearing cash management solution for clients offering FDIC insurance coverage.
Edward Jones: Other asset-based fee revenue consists of revenue sharing, fund adviser fees, cash solutions and Trust Co. fees.

Merrill: Merrill's GWIM business is primarily a fee-based, advice-driven model, with about 30% of its revenue coming from net interest income derived from GWIM clients' loan and deposit balances (period 2025-06-30).

Merrill: Noninterest income, which primarily includes investment and brokerage services income, is driven by asset management fees (reflecting market valuations and AUM flows) and brokerage fees from transactional volume (period 2025-12-31).

Raymond James: Through its Private Client Group segment, Raymond James provides financial planning, investment advisory, and securities transaction services for which it generally charges either asset-based fees (recorded as Asset management and related administrative fees) or sales commissions (recorded as Brokerage revenues).

Raymond James: Raymond James earns asset management and related administrative fees for performing asset management, portfolio management, and related investment services for retail clients for assets invested in fee-based accounts, and earns commissions and distribution-related revenues for brokerage accounts.

Raymond James: The PCG segment also earns servicing fee revenues from third-party mutual fund and annuity companies whose products it distributes and from banks to which it sweeps client cash deposits (RJBDP), and earns net interest on assets segregated for regulatory purposes, margin loans, cash balances, and securities borrowing transactions.

Raymond James: Revenues related to fee-based accounts under administration in PCG are shared between the PCG and Asset Management segments, with the Asset Management segment receiving a higher portion for accounts in managed programs because it performs portfolio management in addition to administrative services.

Raymond James: The majority of assets in PCG fee-based accounts are invested in programs for which Raymond James's financial advisors provide investment advisory services, either on a discretionary or non-discretionary basis.

Schwab: Schwab's revenue on client assets is approximately 21 basis points, per the company's investor-day comparison chart.

Raymond James: Paul Reilly stated that in the RIA and custody services business, Raymond James receives an asset fee, and its net basis points on assets are lower than a pure RIA; part of this is because the service model is different—there is less supervision and compliance responsibility (and therefore less cost), though Raymond James is a higher service model.

Comparison: A direct comparison of revenue yield on client assets between Schwab and advisor-led models cannot be made on this evidence. Schwab provides a revenue-on-client-assets figure of approximately 21 basis points (from its investor-day chart), while no directly comparable revenue-yield figure is reported in the evidence for Morgan Stanley, Edward Jones, or Merrill; Raymond James reports only a qualitative statement about net basis points on assets being lower than a pure RIA in its RIA and custody services business, without a comparable basis-point number. Because the advisor-led firms either report a different quantity (fee rates on fee-based assets, or net interest yield) rather than a firmwide revenue-on-client-assets yield, and because the definitions and scopes differ (Schwab's chart is its own investor-day presentation versus firms' fee rates on subsets of assets), the figures are not comparable on a same-basis basis.

items.text: Edward Jones states the financial services industry continues to evolve technologically, with an increasing number of firms providing enhanced digital experiences for clients, including artificial intelligence and lower-cost computer-based robo-advice.
items.quote: The financial services industry continues to evolve technologically, with an increasing number of firms of all sizes providing enhanced digital experiences for clients, including the utilization of artificial intelligence technologies and lower cost, computer-based "robo-advice."

items.text: Bank of America Private Bank states it uses AI to support advisor capacity, deepen client relationships, and help teams find information faster, and that 93% of Private Bank clients were digitally active in 2025.
items.quote: Bank of America Private Bank uses AI to support advisor capacity, deepen client relationships, and help teams find information faster and more efficiently. In 2025, ninety three percent 93% of Private Bank clients were digitally active

items.text: Morgan Stanley states its technology, including generative artificial intelligence and tokenization, supports evolving client needs across advisor-led, workplace and digital-direct channels.
items.quote: our technology supporting evolving client needs, including generative artificial intelligence and tokenization

items.text: Bank of America states that digital engagement and AI tools continue to expand its capacity to deliver personalized advice at scale.
items.quote: Advisor productivity, disciplined pricing, digital engagement and AI tools continue to expand our capacity to deliver personalized advice at scale.

items.text: Wealthtender research states consumers now expect digital-first experiences even for traditional services like financial advice, and anticipates continued growth in AI tool usage, digital-first communications, and further acceptance of virtual advisor relationships regardless of location.
items.quote: consumers now expecting digital-first experiences even for traditional services like financial advice

items.text: Morgan Stanley states its platform and scale support continued investment in future technology, including AI and digital tools, positioning it to lead as the future of wealth management takes shape.
items.quote: while our scale supports continued investment in future technology, including AI and digital tools. Together, these strengths provide us with a powerful competitive advantage that positions us to lead as the future of wealth management takes shape.

items.text: Schwab states AI is helping it drive both growth and scale and efficiency, and it is continuing to enhance digital experiences across RIA workflows.
items.quote: We'll talk more about our AI progress in a moment, which is helping us drive both growth and scale and efficiency.

items.text: Capgemini World Wealth Report states digital-first clients prefer robo-advisory platforms that deliver seamless, low-cost, self-directed experiences.
items.quote: digital-first clients prefer robo-advisory platforms that deliver seamless, low-cost, self-directed experiences

items.text: Schwab introduced Charley, a new AI-powered assistant that provides U.S. retail clients with conversational access to Schwab's tools and insights, and partnered with Anthropic to bring Claude for Financial Advisors to the independent RIAs it serves.
items.quote: Introduced Charley, a new AI-powered assistant that provides U.S. retail clients with conversational access to Schwab's tools and insights

items.text: Deloitte states clients want advice that is always on and frictionless, and that agentic AI has the potential to flip the adviser workload equation toward building client relationships.
items.quote: Clients want advice that's always on and frictionless, while advisers are busy managing larger, more complex books.

items.text: Accenture research reports 96% of surveyed wealth management professionals say AI is transforming how advice is created for, delivered to, and consumed by clients today.
items.quote: 96% say AI is transforming how advice is created for, delivered to, and consumed by clients today

items.text: Deloitte states that for clients, faster responses, more tailored insights, and more proactive outreach should become minimum standards as agentic AI reshapes how advice is created, packaged and delivered.
items.quote: Faster responses, more tailored insights, and more proactive outreach should become minimum standards.

items.text: Schwab states AI is amplifying its platform advantage, creating more personalized client experiences and greater productivity at scale; a survey cited shows 77% of U.S. investors use AI today while 90%+ prefer human involvement alongside AI.
items.quote: AI is amplifying our platform advantage, creating more personalized client experiences & greater productivity at scale.

items.text: Morgan Stanley states its scale of data gives insights that allow its financial advisors to tailor advice and equip tools to deliver that advice to help clients achieve their goals.
items.quote: It gives us insights given our size and scale that allow our FAs to tailor advice and equip our own tools to deliver that advice to help clients achieve their goals.

items.text: Schwab's Portfolio Insights is a generative AI feature providing a narrative snapshot of a client's portfolio day-change performance and recap of recent news affecting portfolio value.
items.quote: Portfolio Insights (Insights) is a generative artificial intelligence feature designed to provide: (1) a narrative snapshot of a client's Portfolio's Day Change performance

items.text: Deloitte reports Morgan Stanley's AI Debrief automatically summarizes meetings, generates follow-ups, and logs notes into the CRM, freeing advisers to spend more time on client conversations rather than administrative tasks.
items.quote: Morgan Stanley's AI Debrief, for example, automatically summarizes meetings, generates follow-ups, and logs notes into the customer relationship management system, reducing manual documentation and freeing advisers to spend more time on client conversations rather than administrative tasks.

items.text: Wealthtender research finds one-third of prospects prefer online meetings exclusively and do not care about advisor location, enabling virtual service models beyond geographic limitations.
items.quote: One-third of prospects don't care about advisor location, preferring online meetings exclusively.

items.text: Raymond James states the value of true personal relationships cannot be replicated by AI or technology, but will be helped by AI and technology.
items.quote: That can't be replicated by AI or technology, but it will be helped by AI and technology.

items.text: Bank of America describes its view of AI as enhanced intelligence, with teammates remaining critical to delivering services, and notes 2 million customer interactions were handled through the Erica platform on the consumer side alone.
items.quote: Our view of AI is it's enhanced intelligence, that the teammates are going to be critical delivering the services... 2 million customer interactions were handled through the Erika platform just on the consumer side alone.
items.unit: customer interactions handled through Erica platform

items.text: According to Capgemini's World Wealth Report, advances in artificial intelligence are enabling firms to process vast amounts of data and respond to client needs with greater speed and precision, with augmented intelligence enhancing rather than replacing human judgment.
items.quote: Advances in artificial intelligence are accelerating this shift, enabling firms to process vast amounts of data, uncover deeper insights, and respond to client needs with greater speed and precision. At the heart of this shift is augmented intelligence - not technology that replaces human judgment, but technology that enhances it.

items.text: Capgemini's World Wealth Report states the wealth management landscape is shifting from selling products to offering personalized, empathetic advice, defined by how well firms understand clients' lifestyles and aspirations rather than just their assets.
items.quote: The wealth management landscape is shifting from selling products to offering personalized, empathetic advice: future success will be defined by how well firms understand clients' lifestyles and aspirations, rather than just their assets.

items.text: Capgemini's World Wealth Report describes an adaptive AI engine and a personal wealth coach with governed AI copilots that dynamically tailor advice and shift clients from episodic to continuous, context-aware wealth experiences.
items.quote: An Adaptive Experience AI Engine with Knowledge Management as a Service (KMaaS) dynamically tailors content depth, tone, and engagement pathways based on investor personas and life-event context.

items.text: Bank of America's CFO expects the trend to be more technology and more intimacy with customers, with AI becoming more agentic and built into the process rather than delivered by teammates.
items.quote: the trends will be more technology, more intimacy with the customers more agentic versus prompt more built into the process rather than have it be delivered by teammates doing something, it's part of the process, more customers doing more with us

items.text: Raymond James' CEO says the firm uses AI to help financial advisors better serve their clients, whereas many competitors use technology to go direct to clients, bypassing advisors.
items.quote: we're really wanting to use AI to help our financial professionals and our financial advisors better serve their clients, where many of our competitors have used technology and are planning on using AI to essentially try to get around their financial advisors to go direct to their clients.

items.quote: we are harnessing the power of AI in the Schwab way, bringing the best of people and technology and allowing clients to engage the way they prefer.

items.quote: According to research, more than half of our clients are willing to pay for AI financial tools. AI is already driving scale and efficiency in 2 ways... Every one of our sales, service and advice professionals is using AI every day to elevate every interaction they have with clients.
