Bank of America Private Bank states (study published 2026-06-17) it uses AI to support advisor capacity, deepen client relationships, and help teams find information faster, and that 93% of Private Bank clients were digitally active in 2025.

Morgan Stanley states (10-K, period ended 2025-12-31) that its technology, including generative artificial intelligence and tokenization, supports evolving client needs across advisor-led, workplace and digital-direct channels (Wealth Management business segment).

Wealthtender research (published 2025-08-13) states consumers now expect digital-first experiences even for traditional services like financial advice, and anticipates continued growth in AI tool usage, digital-first communications, and further acceptance of virtual advisor relationships regardless of location.

Morgan Stanley states (3Q26 transcript, October 2026) its platform and scale support continued investment in future technology, including AI and digital tools, positioning it to lead as the future of wealth management takes shape.
Schwab states (1Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-03-31) AI is helping it drive both growth and scale and efficiency, and it is continuing to enhance digital experiences across RIA workflows.
Capgemini World Wealth Report (published 2026-06-03) states digital-first clients prefer robo-advisory platforms that deliver seamless, low-cost, self-directed experiences.

Schwab introduced Charley, a new AI-powered assistant that provides U.S. retail clients with conversational access to Schwab's tools and insights, and partnered with Anthropic to bring Claude for Financial Advisors to the independent RIAs it serves (press release, period ended 2026-09-30).

Deloitte (published 2026-05-20) states clients want advice that is always on and frictionless, and that agentic AI has the potential to flip the adviser workload equation toward building client relationships.
Accenture research (published 2025-06-23) reports 96% of surveyed wealth management professionals say AI is transforming how advice is created for, delivered to, and consumed by clients today.

Schwab states (3Q26 deck, 2026 YTD) AI is amplifying its platform advantage, creating more personalized client experiences and greater productivity at scale; a cited survey shows 77% of U.S. investors use AI today while 90%+ prefer human involvement alongside AI.
Morgan Stanley states (3Q26 transcript, October 2026) its scale of data gives insights that allow its financial advisors to tailor advice and equip tools to deliver that advice (Wealth Management).

Deloitte (published 2026-05-20) reports Morgan Stanley's AI Debrief automatically summarizes meetings, generates follow-ups, and logs notes into the CRM, freeing advisers to spend more time on client conversations rather than administrative tasks.

Wealthtender research (published 2025-08-13) finds one-third of prospects prefer online meetings exclusively and do not care about advisor location, enabling virtual service models beyond geographic limitations.
Raymond James states (2Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-06-30) the value of true personal relationships cannot be replicated by AI or technology, but will be helped by AI and technology.

Bank of America (3Q25 transcript, period ended 2025-09-30) describes its view of AI as enhanced intelligence, with teammates remaining critical to delivering services, and notes 2 million customer interactions were handled through the Erica platform on the consumer side alone.

Capgemini's World Wealth Report (published 2026-06-03) states advances in artificial intelligence are enabling firms to process vast amounts of data and respond to client needs with greater speed and precision, with augmented intelligence enhancing rather than replacing human judgment.

Capgemini's World Wealth Report (published 2026-06-03) states the wealth management landscape is shifting from selling products to offering personalized, empathetic advice, defined by how well firms understand clients' lifestyles and aspirations rather than just their assets.

Capgemini's World Wealth Report (published 2026-06-03) describes an adaptive AI engine and a personal wealth coach with governed AI copilots that dynamically tailor advice and shift clients from episodic to continuous, context-aware wealth experiences.

Bank of America's CFO (1Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-03-31) expects the trend to be more technology and more intimacy with customers, with AI becoming more agentic and built into the process rather than delivered by teammates.

Raymond James' CEO (1Q25 transcript, period ended 2025-03-31) says the firm uses AI to help financial advisors better serve their clients, whereas many competitors use technology to go direct to clients, bypassing advisors.

Schwab's CEO (1Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-03-31) says the firm is harnessing AI to bring the best of people and technology and allowing clients to engage the way they prefer, including showing up on AI platforms where investors research.

Schwab's CEO (1Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-03-31) says more than half of clients are willing to pay for AI financial tools, and every sales, service and advice professional uses AI daily to elevate client interactions.

Schwab's CEO (3Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-09-30) says relationships still matter even though AI is fueling growth, and client-facing professionals are armed with tools to serve more clients more effectively.
Bank of America Private Bank states (study published 2026-06-17) it uses AI to support advisor capacity, deepen client relationships, and help teams find information faster and more efficiently.

Edward Jones' investment in Quicken (trade report, published 2026-08-18) is described as addressing the constraint that clients must first understand and organize their financial household before advice can be provided.

Schwab's CEO (2Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-06-30) states more retail clients are seeking holistic financial advice delivered seamlessly on their terms through a combination of people and increasingly AI-enabled technology.

Schwab's CEO (1Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-03-31) states AI opens up new distribution channels and allows the firm to create personalized relationships with clients it had not been able to serve with a person-to-person relationship.
Schwab's CEO (3Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-09-30) states the firm is building a future where its people and AI work together to deliver better outcomes for clients.
A survey (Wealthtender, published 2025-08-13) reports 77% of respondents feel comfortable (very or somewhat) with AI monitoring their accounts for unusual activity to prevent fraud.

Raymond James states (1Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-03-31) it will continue investing in automation, process improvement and AI to create efficiencies, give advisers more time to deepen client relationships and further enhance the client experience.
Schwab's investor day deck (published 2026-05-14) lists 'Professional-led + AI powered planning' as a digital enhancement.

Wealthtender (published 2025-08-13) states its advisor profiles' structured data format makes them more likely to be referenced in Google AI Overviews and AI tools like ChatGPT when prospects ask for advisor recommendations.
Schwab states (3Q26 deck) 90% of accounts are opened digitally and it aims to make Schwab easier to work with through faster, simpler and more digital experiences.
Schwab's CEO (3Q25 transcript, period ended 2025-09-30) states younger investors' top online resource is YouTube and Schwab is the number one financial services firm on YouTube by followers.
Schwab's CEO (4Q25 transcript, period ended 2025-12-31) states the firm leveraged artificial intelligence to serve clients more efficiently in 2025.
Bank of America's CFO (3Q25 transcript, period ended 2025-09-30) states the firm continues to invest in high tech, which drove higher digital engagement, alongside high touch.
Schwab's deck (2Q26, period ended 2026-06-30) describes its value proposition as a powerful combination of people and AI across self-directed and advised solutions.

Capgemini (published 2026-06-03) states advisory roles and incentive structures are being redefined so that relationship managers leverage augmented intelligence to orchestrate experiences across the full wealth ecosystem, coordinating specialists in tax, estate planning, lending, philanthropy, and non-financial value-added services.

Capgemini (published 2026-06-03) states augmentation strengthens human capability by providing better information, faster insights, and broader context, enabling better decisions and more meaningful client engagement, rather than removing tasks.
Capgemini (published 2026-06-03) states augmented intelligence is not technology that replaces human judgment, but technology that enhances it, making every relationship manager more effective.

McKinsey (published 2026-04-08) states the true product of advice, especially in high-net-worth segments, is accountable judgment and behavioral coaching rather than the spreadsheet, which AI cannot replace.
McKinsey (published 2026-04-08) states winners will integrate AI into the operating system of advice in a way that keeps the human relationship at the front end of trust.
Wealthtender states the balance of technological enhancement with human oversight represents the future of financial advice (published 2025-08-13).

Raymond James states it wants to use AI to help financial professionals and advisors better serve their clients, in contrast to competitors using AI to go direct to clients and get around their advisors (1Q25 transcript, period ended 2025-03-31).
Schwab states (3Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-09-30) more than 90 percent of U.S. investors prefer human involvement alongside AI technology.
Schwab created a business development officer role focused solely on growing the business so wealth advisors can focus on their clients (4Q25 transcript, period ended 2025-12-31).
Raymond James states it automates and streamlines processes to free associates and advisors to engage in human-to-human and deepened personal relationships (3Q25 transcript, period ended 2025-09-30).

Bank of America states it will add to the front end where relationship managers matter - the high-touch piece - while taking out activities not directly facing the customer (1Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-03-31).

Raymond James CEO Paul Shoukry said (1Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-03-31) AI will help advisors come up with more bespoke tailored insights, save time on administrative tasks, and allow them to spend more time developing deeply personal relationships with clients.

Raymond James CEO Paul Shoukry said (2Q25 transcript, period ended 2025-06-30) the firm is investing to automate and streamline processes, which frees up advisors to engage human-to-human, deepen relationships and add more value.

Schwab CEO Rick Wurster said (2Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-06-30) the firm's greatest advantage comes from combining people with AI-powered capabilities to create deeper relationships that scale with clients' needs.

Schwab CEO Rick Wurster said (3Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-09-30) relationships still matter and the firm has armed client-facing professionals with tools to help them serve more clients and serve them more effectively.

Raymond James CEO Paul Shoukry said (1Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-03-31) advisors have been and will continue to be expected to provide more holistic and bespoke financial advice to clients over time.
Morgan Stanley CFO Sharon Yeshaya said (trade report, published 2026-10-14) AI is fundamentally changing what teams do, enabling them to work with fewer errors, mistakes and checks.

Raymond James said (trade report, published 2026-09-29) its Private Wealth Guided Portfolios framework is built to sit behind the advisor rather than displace them, preserving the advisor's role as the primary point of contact for each client.

Capgemini research (published 2026-06-03) states the future of wealth management will be defined by personalization at scale underpinned by empathetic advisory relationships, with personalization increasingly embedded through augmented intelligence across every client interaction.

Capgemini research (published 2026-06-03) states the wealth management landscape is shifting from selling products to offering personalized, empathetic advice, with the operating model reaching full maturity through autonomous portfolio delivery and AI-enabled estate and tax planning embedded in client journeys.

Nevis founder Swan predicted (trade report, published 2026-11-03) advisors will have hundreds of AI agents supporting them with a broad range of client services, including building wealth and estate plans and filing taxes.

Schwab's CEO (1Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-03-31) states AI will help deepen existing client relationships by creating personalized and deeper relationships with clients the firm cannot currently serve at scale with one-to-one relationships.

Schwab's CEO (2Q25 transcript, period ended 2025-06-30) states more clients want someone to take over their financial life or at minimum sit by their side and guide them, describing a more holistic, ongoing role for the human advisor.
Raymond James' CEO (1Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-03-31) states technology releases help advisers provide more bespoke advice to a larger number of clients.
Bank of America highlights increasing specialists who support advisors in identifying opportunities as a key accelerant (investor day deck, published 2025-11-05).
Edward Jones states a strategic aspiration to continue investing in technology to scale its ability to provide financial planning to clients (10-K, period ended 2025-12-31).

A research report (Capgemini World Wealth Report, published 2026-06-03) states leading wealth-management firms will distinguish themselves by deploying augmented intelligence to empower relationship managers, reimagine client engagement, and institutionalize personalization at scale.
Schwab's investor materials frame its future offering as a powerful combination of people and AI (2Q26 deck).

Capgemini describes (published 2026-06-03) a target-state where an Adaptive Experience AI Engine dynamically tailors content depth, tone, and engagement pathways based on investor personas and life-event context, enabling journeys to evolve in real time rather than relying on static segmentation.
Schwab's CEO says (2Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-06-30) AI is personalizing client experiences and will personalize more journeys and create more opportunities to deepen relationships over time.

Bank of America's CFO says (3Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-09-30) advisor productivity, digital engagement and AI tools continue to expand the firm's capacity to deliver personalized advice at scale.

Capgemini says (published 2026-06-03) client expectations continue to shift toward more digital, seamless, and highly personalized experiences, while traditional segmentation approaches are showing their limits.
Capgemini describes AI-powered next-best actions aligned to client goals enabling personalized experiences at scale (published 2026-06-03).
Schwab notes (investor day deck, published 2026-05-14) growing demand for holistic advice and rising investor expectations for sophisticated, personalized solutions.

Goldman Sachs Asset Management says (research, published 2025-10-01) retirement strategies should personalize and humanize the retirement experience - an essential evolution in plan design, participant support, and advice.
Capgemini describes (published 2026-06-03) a platform that enables clients to execute investment ideas at their own discretion after advisory conversations, giving them more self-directed control.

Edward Jones' investment in Quicken (trade report, published 2026-08-18) is described as enabling clients to be more proactively and productively engaged in the advice process through a better understanding of their own financial situation.

Deloitte research (published 2026-05-20) states that for clients, the bar should rise quickly, with faster responses, more tailored insights, and more proactive outreach becoming minimum standards as agentic AI reshapes how advice is created and delivered.

Schwab states (2Q25 transcript, period ended 2025-06-30) that over the longer term, AI will meaningfully enhance the way it serves clients and allow it to reach clients in an even more personalized way.
Schwab states (3Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-09-30) that AI will help create more personalized experiences for clients while improving the productivity of the team serving them.

UBS research (published 2026-04-22) states the next generation want advisors with the ability to build rapport with the family and communicate clearly, and partners who can connect them to new ideas, networks, and real-world experiences.

Bank of America states (2Q25 transcript, period ended 2025-06-30) AI is helping relationship managers and advisors search and summarize information, preparing them to deliver personalized planning and personalized pitches to clients.

The World Wealth Report 2026 (published 2026-06-03) expects AI to handle data analysis and pattern recognition so that relationship managers can focus on life planning, deeper advisory work, and judgment calls requiring human empathy and contextual understanding.

The World Wealth Report 2026 (published 2026-06-03) describes a reimagined, AI-powered desktop that delivers a humanlike, empathetic, personalized, and contextual client experience while maintaining trust and human oversight.

Schwab expects to deliver tailored insights to its clients about their investment portfolios through a rollout of portfolio insights, an AI-enabled experience (1Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-03-31).

Schwab's goal (1Q25 transcript, period ended 2025-03-31) is to be the leader for clients who want an omnichannel experience as well as those who may want limited interaction, with AI investments supporting both.

Barclays' Wayne Hawkes states (Capgemini World Wealth Report, published 2026-06-03) that future relationship managers will need to deliver holistic wealth advice to a broader client base, moving away from reactive, product-centric interactions toward intentional, coordinated engagement.

Standard Chartered Bank (Capgemini World Wealth Report, published 2026-06-03) moved away from product-centric conversations toward structured, portfolio-led advisory discussions by enhancing its digital wealth advisory platform.

McKinsey (published 2025-02-10) reports that firms across delivery models are rolling out new advice propositions, with traditionally digital/direct wealth managers rapidly expanding their full-service advice offerings and enhancing the depth and breadth of planning services.

McKinsey states (published 2026-04-08) that a projected shortfall of 90,000 to 110,000 advisors by 2034 makes AI-enabled productivity a necessary capacity lever, and that AI challenges the assumptions that planning is labor-intensive and that regulation provides a barrier to automation.
Deloitte predicts (published 2026-05-20) agentic AI could lift adviser productivity by roughly 30% to 100% by 2032, freeing 25% to 50% of adviser time from lower-value operational work.

Wealthtender (published 2025-08-13) anticipates continued growth in AI tool usage for advisor searches, increasing expectations for digital-first communications, and further acceptance of virtual advisor relationships regardless of geographic location.
Cerulli (published 2025-05-28) finds that a substantial number of clients remain comfortable with commissions and no-fee platforms, and advises firms not to be limited to one engagement option.

Morgan Stanley CFO Sharon Yeshaya states (3Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-09-30) clients either come in directly as fee-based accounts or migrate over time from self-directed, showing the power of the fee-based and advice-led model.

Schwab CEO Rick Wurster states (1Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-03-31) more than half of Schwab's clients are willing to pay for AI financial tools, and that these efforts will create new fee-based offers clients will pay for.

Raymond James CEO Paul Shoukry states (2Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-06-30) client expectations are changing and innovation is accelerating, and that trusted relationships will be helped by AI and technology though not replicated by it.
Schwab positions itself (investor day deck, published 2026-05-14) around a large and growing market for holistic advice, combining AI with human expertise in a one-stop shop.

Trade reporting (published 2026-10-14) states wirehouses Merrill Lynch, Morgan Stanley and Wells Fargo continue to boost and develop sales of alternative investments and artificial intelligence functions for financial advisors in 2026.

Capgemini's World Wealth Report (published 2026-06-03) states that wealth management is shifting from product-centric distribution to empathy-led advice that extends beyond portfolios into the broader context of clients' lives.

Capgemini's roadmap (published 2026-06-03) describes a shift toward AI-augmentation advisory orchestration, moving toward autonomous, tailored portfolio delivery and embedding planning across major life events, with lead relationship managers positioned as experience orchestrators.

Capgemini states (published 2026-06-03) augmented intelligence is the connective tissue of a modern, client-centric operating model, underpinning personalization and consistent delivery of personalized advice.

McKinsey states (published 2026-04-08) AI will quickly replace tasks such as preparation, extraction, drafting, and scenario planning, but replacing tasks is not the same as replacing the advisor's role as the human accountable for judgment, trust, and behavioral coaching.

Bank of America's CFO states (1Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-03-31) the trend will be more technology, more intimacy with customers, more agentic versus prompt, with AI built into the process rather than delivered by teammates.
Cerulli states (published 2025-05-28) that for the past decade financial firms have shifted their compensation models from largely commission-based to an asset-related fee structure.

Morgan Stanley says (4Q25 transcript, period ended 2025-12-31) it is building out fee-based revenues and fee-based assets by introducing new clients to an advice-based model, while also investing in self-directed activity through the E*TRADE franchise and E*TRADE Pro.

Schwab plans to keep all leads of $5 million or less in-house, up from the current $2 million cut-off, a shift described as a seismic shift for many RIAs and gloves off for Schwab's wealth management evolution (trade report, published 2026-08-20; change effective 2027-01-05).

Schwab's investor-day materials (published 2026-05-14) map service and delivery tiers to client segments: self-direct investors get 24/7 service, education and research, and proprietary funds; advice seekers get Wealth Advisory, Advisor Network, and managed accounts; H/UHNW get consultant relationships, dedicated service, and relationship pricing.

Raymond James says its strategy is to keep investing in the people, platforms and capabilities that help its financial professionals deliver more holistic, more personalized advice to clients (1Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-03-31).

Schwab's CEO says (1Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-03-31) advisers continue to win in the marketplace because the fiduciary model works and there is a bull market for advice and convenience, with independent advisers having a great model.

LPL Financial's chief growth officer describes (trade report, published 2026-08-26) the model the firm targets as deeply personal, relationship-based advice with a team approach built on collaboration and accessibility.
Schwab reports (10-Q, period ended 2026-03-31) growth in headcount, including financial consultants and wealth advisors, to support its expanding client base.

Schwab states (1Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-03-31) its financial consultants use an AI capability that, when a client meeting is coming up, summarizes past client interactions, shares recommended actions, records the meeting, and prepares an action-based summary for the client.

Schwab (3Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-09-30) is rolling out an AI-powered thinkorswim assistant and has started a pilot allowing traders to connect to its MCP layer via the LLM of their choice, beginning with Claude.
Schwab (1Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-03-31) uses Wealth.com to bring AI-powered estate planning tools to clients and is working to launch an AI-powered tax planning capability.
Schwab's AI-assisted servicing includes Schwab Assistant v1.0 and Wealth.com AI-powered developer tools (2Q26 deck).
Raymond James launched Rai, a proprietary digital AI operations agent that builds on its service-focused, long-term AI strategy (4Q25 transcript, period ended 2025-12-31).

Raymond James' AI 360 suite of tools (investor day deck, published 2025-06-05) includes prudent process reviews, meeting and CRM notes management, client portfolio analyses, an opportunity dashboard, research and news summaries, statement scanning, regulatory feed summarization, expert service agents, and podcast reviews.

Morgan Stanley's early AI use cases (3Q25 transcript, period ended 2025-09-30) include DevGen AI (which enhances developer efficiency by modernizing code), Parable (an interactive tool that analyzes and summarizes data), and LeadIQ (its AI-powered lead distribution platform matching workplace and self-directed relationships to financial advisors).

Bank of America's AI tools are designed to help its customer relationship managers prepare more thoroughly for client meetings and to let its bankers automate research and presentation materials (2Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-06-30).

Edward Jones' Digital and Data division (10-K, period ended 2025-12-31) provides new tools for branch teams that enable deeper discovery conversations with clients and more comprehensive advice and planning.

Edward Jones (trade report, published 2026-09-30) is developing an end-to-end retirement plan management tool using Aboon Workplace, an AI-native platform that lets advisors find and win retirement plans, covering the workplace retirement plan lifecycle from prospecting to plan servicing.
Capgemini describes an advisor copilot with auto-generated briefs and a consolidated portfolio view among the AI capabilities for client meetings and advisory (published 2026-06-03).

McKinsey (published 2025-02-10) describes gen-AI tools that synthesize information to prepare advisors for client meetings, streamline post-meeting documentation, and automate the development of financial plans and proposals.
Deloitte (published 2026-05-20) describes a stage where AI copilots are embedded in advisor workflows with governance frameworks allowing bounded delegation.
Advisors are advised (Wealthtender, published 2025-08-13) to invest in high-quality video conferencing, digital document signing, and client portal systems as part of their technology investment.

Raymond James said (2Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-06-30) AI and technology will help its financial professionals deliver more holistic and personalized advice while keeping trusted relationships at the center.

Wells Fargo launched an AI-powered tool for its financial advisors that streamlines routine work and helps them access information to better serve clients, described as the first of several planned AI capabilities (trade report, published 2026-10-14).

Bank of America's GWIM segment benefited from new AI-enabled tools that help advisers prepare for client conversations, identify opportunities, and deliver more personalized advice at scale (2Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-06-30).

Morgan Stanley's AI Debrief automatically summarizes meetings, generates follow-ups, and logs notes into the CRM, reducing manual documentation and freeing advisers for client conversations (Deloitte, published 2026-05-20).

With agentic AI (Deloitte, published 2026-05-20), advisers will spend less time on operational tasks and more on higher-value conversations and judgment-heavy moments, while supervising outputs, validating assumptions, and managing exceptions.

Capgemini's Advisory Agent (A³) solution accelerator (published 2026-06-03) consolidates intelligent tools and data into a single integrated interface, surfacing next-best actions and high-value conversations.

Raymond James frames its AI use (3Q25 transcript, period ended 2025-09-30) in three buckets: supporting infrastructure/resiliency/cybersecurity, increasing efficiency and consistency of service, and helping advisors and bankers provide more bespoke and tailored advice.

Schwab is leveraging artificial intelligence (with more than 220 use cases) to help its professionals serve clients more efficiently and is automating high-volume client requests (4Q25 transcript, period ended 2025-12-31).

Schwab said (2Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-06-30) AI is becoming more embedded in its omnichannel experience, personalizing client experiences and enhancing productivity, with rollout of Portfolio Insights and an employee pilot of Schwab Assistant.

Schwab's Portfolio Insights is a generative AI feature providing a narrative snapshot of a client's portfolio day-change performance, a recap of news on top S&P 500 movers, and snippets of expert content (press release, period ended 2026-06-30).

Bank of America said (2Q25 transcript, period ended 2025-06-30) AI is helping wealth management relationship managers and advisors search and summarize information to prepare personalized planning and pitches, with copilots organizing the prospecting process.

Merrill launched Tax Efficient Transition Service and Dollar Cost Averaging Service, combining automation with professional portfolio oversight to streamline portfolio transitions and cash deployment into managed strategies (press release, published 2026-09-15).

The advisor industry has built account aggregation and financial dashboard tools (trade report, published 2026-08-18), including eMoney's personal financial management dashboard, Envestnet's Yodlee with MoneyGuide, and RightCapital's dashboard and budgeting tools.

Capgemini describes augmented intelligence as using data and AI-driven insights to enhance relationship manager judgment, surface behavioral signals, anticipate needs, and automate workflows (published 2026-06-03).
Raymond James is investing to equip advisers with private wealth tools and resources, and continuing to invest in automation, process improvement, and AI (2Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-06-30).

Consumer research (Wealthtender, published 2025-08-13) shows high comfort with AI for meeting transcription (74%), market data analysis (74%), fraud monitoring (77%), and communication drafting (68%), and moderate comfort for financial planning, risk assessment, and tax optimization.

Standard Chartered Bank's MyWealth advisor platform (Capgemini World Wealth Report, published 2026-06-03) gives relationship managers a consolidated view of client holdings and risk profiles, generates portfolio insights and investment ideas, and uses generative AI to draft client communications.

According to Capgemini's World Wealth Report (published 2026-06-03), in the 'Now' horizon the priority is establishing the intelligence foundation by identifying the right data and deploying AI-driven productivity tools.

Raymond James lists advisor tools (investor day deck, published 2025-06-05) including RJnet & Advisor Access GenAI Search, Zoom AI Meeting Summaries, Advisor Access Recommended Apps, GenAI Search, Microsoft CoPilot, and the NASH Platform.

Schwab's CEO said (1Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-03-31) the firm is working with a leading AI agent firm, is offering an AI-powered estate planning capability from wealth.com and will do the same with tax, and that every sales, service and advice professional is using AI every day.

Bank of America lists accelerants (investor day deck, published 2025-11-05) including investing in transition tools, deploying personalization capabilities, increasing specialists supporting advisors, and expanding UHNW and CIO portfolio management solutions.

Raymond James' CEO said (1Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-03-31) the firm spent $1.1 billion on technology and AI from adviser tools to client tools, and that advisers will need technology, including AI, to provide more holistic and bespoke financial advice.
Raymond James' CEO said (4Q25 transcript, period ended 2025-12-31) the firm launched 'Rai', a play on Raymond James.

A survey (Wealthtender, published 2025-08-13) found respondents are comfortable with AI monitoring accounts for fraud (77%), analyzing market data to inform recommendations (74%), drafting routine client communications (74%), and recording/transcribing meetings (74%).
Schwab's CEO said (2Q25 transcript, period ended 2025-06-30) the firm is enhancing tax, trust and estate capabilities, including plans to offer wealth.com's estate planning tools to retail clients.

Cerulli estimates (published 2026-03-25) middle-market and mass-affluent households with between $100,000 and $2 million in financial assets grew their wealth from $14 trillion to $25 trillion between 2013 and 2025, a $25 trillion market of 46.9 million households that seeks involved advisor relationships.

Cerulli reports (published 2026-03-25) opportunities for providers to engage new clients drop sharply as prospects age, from 44% among the affluent under 30 to 24% among those in their 50s, and that providers need to engage prospects earlier.

Cerulli finds (published 2026-04-09) affluent investors' willingness to pay for financial advice rose to 68% in 2025 from 38% in 2010, attributed in part to greater accessibility of financial advice, fee compression, and proliferation of fiduciary advice.

Capgemini states (published 2026-06-03) the future of wealth management will be defined by personalization at scale, democratizing excellence in advice through augmented intelligence across every client interaction.
Capgemini cites (published 2026-06-03) the ongoing democratization of private markets as one of the innovations shaping the future of wealth management.
Schwab states (10-K, period ended 2025-12-31) its advisory solutions, including discretionary and non-discretionary services, have minimum investments starting at $5,000.
Schwab's retail value proposition (investor day deck, published 2026-05-14) combines best-in-class digital platforms with no minimums or commissions.
Schwab cites (investor day deck, published 2026-05-14) that 68% of affluent investors want and are willing to pay for advice.

Morgan Stanley states (2Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-06-30) it can offer financial advice broadly for different types of individuals at different points in their life cycle, and match advisers to the right clients using technology.
Morgan Stanley states (1Q25 transcript, period ended 2025-03-31) it is working toward a more democratized offering of alternatives across its platform to its retail client base.
Schwab states (4Q25 transcript, period ended 2025-12-31) it is winning with investors of all ages, wealth tiers, and time horizons, with about one-third of new clients affluent.
Morgan Stanley states (4Q24 transcript, period ended 2024-12-31) investments in its self-directed and Workplace channels drive its client acquisition funnel, reaching over 19 million relationships.

McKinsey's survey of US investors indicates that the share of investors seeking more holistic advice grew from 29% in 2018 to 52% in 2023, as client needs become more complex across planning services and products (published 2025-02-10).

McKinsey research (published 2026-04-08) states that while nearly 80% of affluent households still prefer a human relationship, an AI takeover might be possible for standardized, lower-touch service models and for younger clients who are increasingly comfortable with AI-only interfaces.

Capgemini states (published 2026-06-03) that in the 'Soon' horizon, competitive differentiation begins as firms evolve to democratize access to alternative investments and offer specialized value-added services.

Schwab states (10-K, period ended 2025-12-31) it serves a broad spectrum of individual investors, from those just beginning their investing journey to clients with substantial and complex wealth management needs, with Schwab Private Client Services for clients with $1 million to $10 million and Schwab Private Wealth Services for clients with more than $10 million.

Schwab's CEO states (2Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-06-30) that just 5% of Schwab retail households are in a fee-based advice solution, while 31% of Schwab clients said they are willing to pay for advice, describing an unmatched conversion funnel into advice from its self-directed investor base.
Schwab's CEO states (4Q25 transcript, period ended 2025-12-31) the Forge acquisition will help provide clients with multiple ways to access alternatives while democratizing private investing.

Bank of America states (investor day deck, published 2025-11-05) its wealth management businesses are positioned to serve clients through all stages of the wealth continuum, from Mass Market (<$500K) through Mass Affluent ($500K-$1MM), High Net Worth ($1MM-$10MM) to Ultra High Net Worth ($10MM+).

Edward Jones states (10-K, period ended 2025-12-31) its initiatives include targeting new clients: High Net Worth (attracting and serving high net worth clients), Workplace (connecting local business owners and employees with financial solutions), and a new digital platform focused on attracting and retaining Next Generation investors.

Morgan Stanley's Core Client Relationships (Advisor-Led, Workplace, and Self-Directed) grew from approximately 13 million in 2020 to approximately 20 million in 2025 (strategic update deck, published 2026-01-15).

Deloitte states (published 2026-05-20) that agentic AI presents a real opportunity to address client experience, with faster responses, more tailored insights, and more proactive outreach becoming minimum standards.

Edward Jones states (10-K, period ended 2025-12-31) its strategic ambition is to help tens of millions of investors achieve financial fulfillment through personalized, comprehensive planning and trusted advice, and it aspires to attract and serve new client segments.

Edward Jones states (10-Q, period ended 2025-06-27) it is committed to helping improve the financial wellness of tens of millions of long-term investors across North America by providing comprehensive, personalized planning and professional advice.
According to Schwab CEO Rick Wurster (trade report, published 2026-08-20), only 5% of Schwab retail households are in fee-based advice, as of 2026-07-21.

Schwab's investor day materials list distinct client segments - self-directed investors, traders, younger investors, advice seekers, and high/ultra-high net worth - each served with tailored offerings, including Wealth Advisory and Advisor Network for advice seekers and consultant relationships and dedicated service for H/UHNW clients (published 2026-05-14).

Schwab describes a large and growing market for holistic advice and states it has a proven ability to grow adoption of its solutions across an engaged and loyal client base (investor day deck, published 2026-05-14).

Merrill Wealth Management's advisory business (BAC 10-K, period ended 2025-12-31) provides a high-touch client experience through a network of financial advisors focused on clients with over $250,000 in total investable assets, while Bank of America Private Bank and Private Wealth Management target high net worth and ultra high net worth clients.

Raymond James' Private Wealth Advisor designation program (trade report, published 2026-09-29) targets advisors who specialize in high-net-worth clients, generally defined as those with at least $5 million in investable assets.

Capgemini's World Wealth Report states (published 2026-06-03) that AI handles data analysis and pattern recognition from client conversations so that relationship managers can focus on life planning and deeper advisory work requiring human judgment.

Capgemini's World Wealth Report describes (published 2026-06-03) a large wealth firm implementing a reimagined AI-powered desktop that delivers a humanlike, empathetic, personalized, and contextual client experience.

Schwab's CEO describes (3Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-09-30) Charley, an AI-powered assistant that gives retail clients conversational access to Schwab's tools and insights and can take action on a client's behalf for administrative tasks such as changing an address.

A WealthTender survey (published 2025-08-13) finds many clients want their advisor to be local but express a preference for meetings to be conducted online, and that people are comfortable when AI enhances human capabilities rather than replacing human judgment.
Bank of America's investor day deck lists deploying personalization capabilities based on client preferences as a key accelerant (published 2025-11-05).

Raymond James's CEO states (2Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-06-30) the firm will invest in people, platforms and capabilities that help financial professionals deliver more holistic and personalized advice, while noting client relationships will be helped by AI and technology.

Edward Jones's 10-K states its strategic ambition is to help investors achieve financial fulfillment through personalized, comprehensive planning and trusted advice, investing in technology to scale financial planning (period ended 2025-12-31).

Capgemini states its Business-Ready Data for AI foundation (published 2026-06-03) enables accurate recommendations that balance personalization with suitability and delivers trusted AI insights to provide the right advice at the right time.

Edward Jones states (10-K, period ended 2025-12-31) that in its Guided Solutions client-directed advisory program, clients retain control over investment decisions while financial advisors guide them through identifying goals and selecting a portfolio objective.
Bank of America states (3Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-09-30) it keeps customers in control of decisions and the human in the loop before money is moved out of their accounts.
Schwab states (3Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-09-30) it is blocking unauthorized AI agents that try to log in on behalf of clients, to protect clients and the firm.
Raymond James states (3Q25 transcript, period ended 2025-09-30) it uses AI to help its financial advisors and bankers provide more bespoke and tailored advice to a larger number of clients.
Merrill states (press release, published 2026-09-15) its new Tax Efficient Transition Service and Dollar Cost Averaging Service help support more personalized investment strategies for clients.

Raymond James states (2Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-06-30) it is investing to equip advisers and associates with private wealth tools and resources to deliver deeper, more tailored advice while keeping personal relationships at the center.
Edward Jones states (10-K, period ended 2025-12-31) its Financial Planning Services initiative gives clients a more personalized experience with additional planning capabilities.
Morgan Stanley states (3Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-09-30) its data and scale give insights that allow its financial advisors to tailor advice and equip its tools to deliver that advice.

Capgemini World Wealth Report states (published 2026-06-03) augmented intelligence uses data and AI-driven insights to enhance relationship manager judgment and ensure the consistent delivery of personalized advice across the firm.

A financial advisor who moved to independence (launching through LPL) stated (trade report, published 2026-10-14) independence gives flexibility to tailor the approach around each family's unique needs and goals.

Capgemini research (published 2026-06-03) states the future of wealth management will be defined by personalization at scale, and that engagement models will evolve so life transitions, liquidity events, and behavioral signals determine when and how firms interact with clients, replacing calendar-driven review cycles with relevance-driven ones.

Schwab's CEO states (2Q25 transcript, period ended 2025-06-30) more and more clients want someone to essentially take over their financial life or, at a minimum, sit by their side and help guide them through their financial life.

Raymond James' CEO states (1Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-03-31) advisers have been and will continue to be expected to provide more holistic and bespoke financial advice to clients over time, which requires the firm to provide technology where AI can help.
Raymond James' CEO states (3Q25 transcript, period ended 2025-09-30) the firm's AI investments create efficiency and higher quality advice to clients through the use of data-driven insights.

Schwab Advisor Services states (trade report, published 2026-10-23) the Syntax Direct/iRebal integration gives RIAs control over creating personalized portfolios at scale, letting an advisor build a custom index and put it to work across client accounts without a manual handoff.
McKinsey projects (published 2025-02-10) that, based on current trends, US advisor supply will be 290 thousand advisors by 2034.
McKinsey projects (published 2025-02-10) advisor headcount will decline by about 0.2 percent annually (advisor industry).

Bank of America expects (3Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-09-30) its headcount to be down by 3,000, or 1.5% year-over-year in 2027, with managers down about 5%, while production teammates doing client-facing work are up year-over-year.
Bank of America's CEO expects (4Q25 transcript, period ended 2025-12-31) its headcount to come down during 2026, achieved through attrition rather than hiring.

Schwab is continuing to hire financial consultants and wealth advisers (1Q26 transcript, period ended 2026-03-31) while expanding its branch footprint, with about a dozen new branches planned for 2026.
Schwab plans to hire hundreds of new financial consultants and expand its physical branch network in the year ahead (4Q24 transcript, period ended 2024-12-31) covering 2025.

Raymond James ended the fiscal year (period ended 2025-09-30) with a record number of financial advisors, 2% higher than the prior year, and remains optimistic about growth based on a robust recruiting pipeline and commitments to join in coming quarters.
Raymond James ended the fiscal year (period ended 2025-09-30) with a record 8,943 financial advisors.

Morgan Stanley's March workforce management action impacted approximately 2% of its global workforce, with $61 million of severance costs in the Wealth Management segment (press release, period ended 2026-09-30, action dated 2026-03-31).
Bank of America's investor day deck projects its Private Client Advisors to reach a medium-term target of 700, up from 545 in 3Q25 and 482 in 2019 (published 2025-11-05).
McKinsey & Co. projects a shortfall of 90,000 to 110,000 advisors by 2034 at current productivity levels (trade report, published 2026-11-13).
Deloitte states (published 2026-05-20) wealth management faces a widening adviser shortage against a backdrop of a US$124 trillion generational wealth transfer.

Deloitte states (published 2026-05-20) the advice delivery model may shift away from individual effort toward apprenticeship, specialization, and technology leverage, driving more teaming, greater practice consolidation, and a higher premium on leaders who can mentor, develop clients, and scale larger teams.

caveats: All sources - How advisor headcount and staffing levels are projected to change with future advice delivery: the figures cover different bases and are not one series: Bank of America: 2027; Schwab: 2025, 2026; Raymond James: 2025-09-30; Morgan Stanley (global workforce): 2026-03-31; whole firm: 2034. The break is flagged, not smoothed.

No single firm's claims are comparable against the others for a definitive ranking.

a1.all.label: fact

items.text: McKinsey (PriceMetrix) reports that after a period of fee compression for advisory relationships from 2013 to 2018, advisory fee rates have stabilized.
items.quote: After a period of fee compression for advisory relationships from 2013 to 2018, fee rates have stabilized, according to PriceMetrix by McKinsey.

items.text: McKinsey believes fee pressure will be uneven, manifesting as demands for transparency and unbundled pricing rather than a blanket reduction in basis points.
items.quote: We believe fee pressure will be uneven, manifesting as demands for transparency and unbundled pricing rather than a blanket reduction in basis points.

items.text: Deloitte states that while lower cost-to-serve can expand margins for firms that maintain pricing, competitive pressure may compress fees as planning outputs become easier to compare.
items.quote: Lower cost-to-serve can expand margins for firms that execute and maintain pricing. At the same time, competitive pressure may compress fees as planning outputs become easier to compare.

items.text: Edward Jones states that significant reductions in mutual fund and insurance revenues are driven in large part by the ongoing fee compression that has occurred across the mutual fund industry in recent years.
items.quote: driven in large part by the ongoing fee compression that has occurred across the mutual fund industry in recent years

items.text: Cerulli states that for the past decade, financial firms have shifted their compensation models from largely commission-based to an asset-related fee structure.
items.quote: For the past decade, financial firms have shifted their compensation models from largely commission-based to an asset-related fee structure.

items.text: Raymond James states that regulatory requirements have resulted in greater price transparency, leading to price competition and decreased trading margins.
items.quote: regulatory requirements have resulted in greater price transparency, leading to price competition and decreased trading margins.

items.text: Cerulli attributes the increased willingness to pay for advice in part to continued fee compression across both advisors and product fees.
items.quote: continued fee compression across both advisors and product fees

items.text: Raymond James states that the market environment in recent years has resulted in a shift to passive investment products, which generate lower fees than actively managed products.
items.quote: the market environment in recent years has resulted in a shift to passive investment products, which generate lower fees than actively managed products.

items.text: A Wealthtender survey found that nearly three-quarters (73%) of survey participants said transparency in fees and services is crucial for establishing an advisor's credibility.
items.quote: Nearly three-quarters (73%) of survey participants said transparency in fees and services is crucial for establishing an advisor's credibility.

items.text: Industry trade coverage states that the broader debate over cash sweep transparency and pricing remains a live issue, with the SEC's sustained focus on sweep disclosures and litigation over client yields.
items.quote: the broader debate over cash sweep transparency and pricing remains a live issue. The SEC's sustained focus on sweep disclosures, combined with a wave of litigation against major firms over allegedly low client yields

items.text: McKinsey reports that industry leaders are worried whether the rapid commoditization of technical expertise will erode the barriers to entry that have historically protected high-margin advisory fees.
items.quote: Industry leaders are worried whether the rapid commoditization of technical expertise will erode the barriers to entry that have historically protected high-margin advisory fees.

items.text: Trade press reports an industry-wide shift to data fees and ETF platform/revenue-sharing fees, with Fidelity introducing a $100 ticket charge in March 2024 on trades of funds that refused to pay shelf-space fees, and UBS and Wells Fargo introducing data fees in the mid-2010s and 2020 respectively; an analyst predicted the widespread adoption of data fees to offset declining transaction revenue.
items.quote: Fidelity introduced ETF platform and revenue sharing fees in March 2024 – including a $100 ticket charge on trades of funds that refused to pay shelf-space fees – and major wires, including UBS and Wells Fargo introduced data fees in the mid-2010s, and 2020, respectively. Pirker first predicted the widespread adoption of data fees to offset declining transaction revenue in 2019

items.text: Trade press reports Merrill Lynch is creating new 'data' and 'shelf' fees, creating fee bundles on up to $1.4 billion for third-party managers to pay in exchange for getting listed and recommended by its brokers.
items.quote: it is creating fees for third-party managers to pay – fee bundles on up to $1.4 billion – to give itself the incentive not to put itself and few close manager friends first all the time

items.text: Research holds that if AI collapses the marginal cost of generating tax analysis, scenario modeling, portfolio commentary and meeting documentation, then operating leverage, advisor capacity and fee durability require rigorous reexamination.
items.quote: If the marginal cost of generating tax analysis, scenario modeling, portfolio commentary, and meeting documentation collapses, then operating leverage, advisor capacity, and fee durability require rigorous reexamination.

items.text: Schwab states it periodically adjusts fees for advisory services, expense ratios on funds/ETFs, trade commission rates and other pricing to sustain its competitive position, citing increased price competition such as reduced commissions, higher deposit rates and reduced mutual fund or ETF expense ratios.
items.quote: Increased price competition from other financial services firms to attract clients, such as reduced commissions, higher deposit rates, reduced mutual fund or ETF expense ratios, or the increased use of incentives, could impact our results of operations and financial condition.

items.text: A survey found just over 38% of people consider lack of transparency about fees or commissions a major red flag when evaluating a financial advisor.
items.quote: Just over 38% of people consider lack of transparency about fees or commissions a major red flag.

items.text: A survey found 'Fee structure and pricing' was cited by 61.8% of respondents as the most helpful information when looking for a financial advisor.
items.quote:
Fee structure and pricing
61.80%

items.text: Trade press reports the SEC has focused on cash sweep account options for several years, including a $187 million settlement with Charles Schwab in 2022 over misleading disclosures related to its robo-advisor cash program, and more recently closed its probe into LPL's cash sweep program without enforcement action.
items.quote: The SEC has been focused on cash sweep account options for several years, with sizable settlements that included a $187 million agreement with Charles Schwab in 2022 over misleading disclosures related to its robo-advisor cash program.

items.text: In June 2022 Schwab and its affiliate settled an SEC matter over historical disclosures and marketing of the Schwab Intelligent Portfolios program, with the SEC finding CS&Co. made false and misleading statements about cash allocations, including its conflict of interest and the negative effect of cash allocations on performance.
items.quote: The SEC found that CS&Co. made false and misleading statements in Form ADV Part 2A brochures about the cash allocations in Schwab Intelligent Portfolios accounts

items.text: Schwab notes the SEC's decision to lower exchange processing fees to zero beginning in mid-May 2025.
items.quote: the SEC's decision to lower exchange processing fees to zero beginning in mid-May

items.quote: RPAG will provide the benchmarking, fee comparisons and ongoing management of the retirement plans.

items.quote: you may be assessed other trading related costs (mark-ups, markdowns and/or other fees and charges) by the other broker-dealer. Those costs are in addition to your Program fees

a2.all.reason: The passages state industry-level findings and trends about how pricing transparency and fee structures are changing across wealth management; these directly answer the sub-question about the industry-wide direction on pricing transparency.

a3.all.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley states that the SEC's Regulation Best Interest requires broker-dealers to act in the 'best interest' of retail customers at the time a recommendation is made without placing the financial or other interests of the broker-dealer ahead of the interest of the retail customer.
items.quote: the SEC's "Regulation Best Interest," which requires broker-dealers to act in the "best interest" of retail customers at the time a recommendation is made without placing the financial or other interests of the broker-dealer ahead of the interest of the retail customer.

items.text: Raymond James states that under the Dodd-Frank Act the SEC adopted Regulation Best Interest, which requires a broker-dealer to act in the best interest of a retail client when making a recommendation, and Form CRS, which requires retail investors be given a brief summary document with information about the relationship, and that various states have proposed or adopted laws imposing new standards of conduct on broker-dealers.
items.quote: Regulation Best Interest requires a broker-dealer to act in the best interest of a retail client when making a recommendation to that client of any securities transaction or investment strategy involving securities. Form CRS requires that broker-dealers and investment advisers provide retail investors with a brief summary document containing simple, easy-to-understand information about the nature of the relationship between the parties.

items.text: Edward Jones states it is subject to the SEC rule requiring registered investment advisers and broker-dealers to deliver a Form CRS Relationship Summary informing clients of the types of relationships offered, the applicable standards of care, and information on fees, costs, conflicts of interest, and legal and disciplinary history.
items.quote: Edward Jones is also subject to the SEC rule requiring registered investment advisers and broker-dealers to deliver a Form CRS Relationship Summary to their clients informing them of the types of client relationships offered, together with the applicable standards of care, and information on fees, costs, conflicts of interest, and legal and disciplinary history.

items.text: Raymond James states that in April 2024 the Department of Labor issued a final rule significantly expanding the definition of 'investment advice fiduciary' under ERISA and finalized amendments to several class prohibited transaction exemptions that exempt certain compensation arrangements otherwise prohibited, and that if the rules become effective compliance will require altering certain business practices and imposing additional costs.
items.quote: In April 2024, the Department of Labor ("DOL") issued a final rule significantly expanding the definition of "investment advice fiduciary" under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974... the DOL also finalized amendments to several class prohibited transaction exemptions ("PTE"), which exempt certain compensation arrangements that would otherwise be prohibited... we expect compliance will require us to alter certain of our business practices and impose additional costs.

items.text: Schwab states that in March 2026 federal district courts reached final resolutions on pending litigation and formally vacated the U.S. Department of Labor's April 2024 final rule to broaden the definition of 'fiduciary' under ERISA, and the rule was removed from the Code of Federal Regulations.
items.quote: In March 2026, federal district courts reached final resolutions on pending litigation and formally vacated the U.S. Department of Labor's April 2024 final rule to broaden the definition of "fiduciary" under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974. Following the courts' ruling, the U.S. Department of Labor's Employee Benefits Security Administration removed the rule from the Code of Federal Regulations.

items.text: Morgan Stanley states that under Department of Labor regulations under Section 408(b)(2) of ERISA, MSWM is required to provide certain information regarding its services and compensation to assist fiduciaries and plan sponsors in assessing the reasonableness of their plan's contracts or arrangements, including the reasonableness of its compensation.
items.quote: In accordance with Department of Labor regulations under Section 408(b)(2) of ERISA, MSWM is required to provide certain information regarding our services and compensation to assist fiduciaries and plan sponsors... in assessing the reasonableness of their plan's contracts or arrangements with us, including the reasonableness of our compensation.

items.text: Merrill Lynch states that under Department of Labor regulations under Section 408(b)(2) of ERISA it is required to provide certain information regarding its services and compensation to assist fiduciaries and plan sponsors of retirement accounts subject to ERISA in assessing the reasonableness of compensation.
items.quote: In accordance with Department of Labor regulations under Section 408(b)(2) of ERISA, we are required to provide certain information regarding our services and compensation to assist fiduciaries and plan sponsors... in assessing the reasonableness of their plan's contracts or arrangements with us, including the reasonableness of our compensation.

items.text: Raymond James states that beginning in August 2024 the SEC's Division of Enforcement requested information regarding its practices related to cash sweep programs for investment advisory clients, and that class action lawsuits were filed alleging breach of fiduciary duties with regard to rates paid to clients in its cash sweep programs.
items.quote: beginning in August 2024, the SEC's Division of Enforcement requested information regarding our practices related to cash sweep programs for investment advisory clients and has reportedly conducted similar reviews at other financial institutions... alleging, among other things, that the firm breached its fiduciary duties or agreements with regard to rates paid to clients in our cash sweep programs.

items.text: Trade press reports that the SEC has been focused on cash sweep account options for several years, with sizable settlements including a $187 million agreement with Charles Schwab in 2022 over misleading disclosures related to its robo-advisor cash program, and that the SEC closed its probe into LPL's cash sweep program without enforcement action in January 2026.
items.quote: The SEC has been focused on cash sweep account options for several years, with sizable settlements that included a $187 million agreement with Charles Schwab in 2022 over misleading disclosures related to its robo-advisor cash program.
items.scope: Charles Schwab robo-advisor cash program settlement

items.text: Merrill Lynch states that on April 3, 2023 the SEC issued an administrative order finding MLPF&S violated the Advisers Act because wrap fee advisory program agreements and ADV brochures contained a material misstatement by failing to disclose an additional 'production credit' fee on foreign currency exchanges, resulting in a penalty totaling $9,694,714.
items.quote: wrap fee advisory program agreements and ADV brochures contained a material misstatement because, while disclosing that MLPF&S charged a mark-up or markdown on foreign currency exchanges, the disclosure did not also state that an additional fee referred to as a production credit was also charged... payment of disgorgement, prejudgment interest and a civil penalty totaling $9,694,714.

items.text: Schwab states the SEC found that CS&Co. made false and misleading statements in Form ADV Part 2A brochures about the cash allocations in Schwab Intelligent Portfolios accounts, including about its conflict of interest in setting the cash allocations and the negative effect of the cash allocations on performance.
items.quote: The SEC found that CS&Co. made false and misleading statements in Form ADV Part 2A brochures about the cash allocations in Schwab Intelligent Portfolios accounts, in particular about: CS&Co.'s conflict of interest in setting the cash allocations; the influence of this conflict of interest on the size of the cash allocations; and the negative effect of the cash allocations on performance...

items.text: Trade press reports the SEC has targeted advisors and firms in ongoing 'sweeps' over misleading advertising, with wealth management firms cited for failing to comply with Rule 206(4)-1 (the Marketing Rule) governing how third-party ratings are used, including a September 2024 sweep settling against nine RIAs for a combined $1.24 million in fines.
items.quote: the SEC has targeted advisors and firms in ongoing "sweeps" to ferret out misleading advertising. Wealth management firms have been cited for failing to comply with the rules governing how third-party ratings are used under Rule 206(4)-1 (The Marketing Rule)... In a Sept. 2024 sweep, the SEC investigated and settled cases against nine registered investment advisers (RIAs) for a combined $1.24 million in fines.

items.text: FINRA's oversight materials reference SEC Rule 606 of Regulation NMS disclosures on order handling and routing, including responses to frequently asked questions and a risk alert on observations related to Rule 606 disclosures.
items.quote: Responses to Frequently Asked Questions Concerning Rule 606 of Regulation NMS (updated June 26, 2024)... Division of Examinations Risk Alert: Observations Related to Regulation NMS Rule 606 Disclosures (Nov. 10, 2022)... SEC Adopts Rules That Increase Information Brokers Must Provide to Investors on Order Handling (Nov. 2, 2018)

items.text: Schwab states that on June 12, 2025 the SEC withdrew certain notices of proposed rulemaking, including the December 2022 equity market structure rule proposals 'Order Competition Rule' and 'Regulation Best Execution', which the company had been evaluating.
items.quote: On June 12, 2025, the SEC withdrew certain notices of proposed rulemaking issued between March 2022 and November 2023... The withdrawn proposals included the December 2022 equity market structure rule proposals, "Order Competition Rule" and "Regulation Best Execution".

items.text: The SEC's sustained focus on cash sweep disclosures, combined with litigation against major firms over allegedly low client yields on uninvested cash, is keeping cash sweep transparency and pricing a live compliance issue across the independent channel.
items.quote: The SEC's sustained focus on sweep disclosures, combined with a wave of litigation against major firms over allegedly low client yields, means that the question of who benefits from rising rates on uninvested cash is unlikely to fade from client conversations any time soon.

items.text: State securities regulators (NASAA) settled with Wells Fargo and Merrill Lynch over charges of unreasonable commissions on small-dollar retail equity transactions, requiring a combined $4.4 million settlement with restitution on excess commissions over a five-year period.
items.quote: Wells Fargo and Merrill have agreed to a combined $4.4 million settlement with state securities regulators over charges of unreasonable commissions on small-dollar retail equity transactions

items.text: Schwab states it is required under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940 to provide clients disclosure brochures describing how services work, the fees charged, and important conflicts of interest, and to update these brochures and notify clients of material changes.
items.quote: Charles Schwab & Co., Inc. ("CS&Co.") is required under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940 (the "Advisers Act") to provide clients with disclosure brochures that describe our investment advisory and financial planning services, including how these services work, the fees charged, and important conflicts of interest.

Why it might matter: the source states MSSB's advisory-client relationships are subject to fiduciary and other obligations, and that the SEC and other supervisory bodies have broad administrative powers to address non-compliance, including restricting MSSB from carrying on investment advisory and asset management activities.

Morgan Stanley's 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states it has experienced, and may continue to experience, pricing pressures as competitors seek to gain market share by reducing prices and fees, paying higher deposit rates, eliminating commissions or offering more favorable terms. Why it might matter: certain competitors may be subject to different and, in some cases, less stringent, legal and regulatory regimes than the firm, thereby putting it at a competitive disadvantage.

Morgan Stanley's 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states it competes on several factors including price, and that the financial services industry is intensely competitive. Why it might matter: the firm has experienced, and will likely continue to experience, increased competition driven by established financial services firms and emerging firms, including non-financial companies.

FINRA's oversight materials (December 9, 2025) reference SEC Rule 606 of Regulation NMS disclosures on order handling and routing, including responses to frequently asked questions and a risk alert on observations related to Rule 606 disclosures. Raymond James's 10-K (period ended September 30, 2025) states that under the Dodd-Frank Act the SEC adopted Regulation Best Interest, which requires a broker-dealer to act in the best interest of a retail client when making a recommendation, and Form CRS, which requires retail investors be given a brief summary document with information about the relationship, and that various states have proposed or adopted laws imposing new standards of conduct on broker-dealers. Why it might matter: the passage describes a package of rule-makings and interpretations related to the provision of advice by broker-dealers and investment advisers, including Regulation Best Interest and Form CRS.

Raymond James's 10-K (period ended September 30, 2025) states that in April 2024 the Department of Labor issued a final rule significantly expanding the definition of investment advice fiduciary under ERISA and finalized amendments to several class prohibited transaction exemptions that exempt certain compensation arrangements otherwise prohibited, and that if the rules become effective compliance will require altering certain business practices and imposing additional costs. Why it might matter: the passage notes the UK Consumer Duty requires firms to act to deliver good outcomes for retail customers with respect to products and services, price and value, consumer understanding, and consumer support.

Raymond James's 10-K (period ended September 30, 2025) states that regulatory requirements have produced greater price transparency, driving price competition and lower trading margins, and that competitors seek market share by cutting fees, commissions or margins. Why it might matter: trading margins have been further compressed by the shift from high- to low-touch services over time, which has created additional competitive pressure.

Raymond James's 10-K (period ended September 30, 2025) states it competes with higher deposit rates to attract client cash balances, which could result in pricing pressure. Why it might matter: competition to attract clients or trading volume, through direct-to-investor online financial services, could result in pricing pressure or otherwise adversely impact the business.

Fidelity's 2025 Investor Insights Study (October 9, 2025) found that high-net-worth next-generation households seek transparency in advisor compensation, along with broader life guidance and emerging investment products. Why it might matter: advisors must adapt to these shifting dynamics to effectively serve the distinctive demands of this generation, which is navigating unique life stages and ambitious financial goals.

A WealthTender survey (August 13, 2025) found nearly half (48%) of participants cited pricing and overall anticipated costs among the top three factors for choosing one advisor over another, framed as a need for transparent, reasonable pricing rather than the lowest cost. Why it might matter: transparent, reasonable pricing gives clients peace of mind and helps them budget.

A survey (2025) found that 73% of people consider fee transparency the most important trust factor, and pricing is the top factor in final advisor selection. Why it might matter: lack of fee transparency was identified as a red flag by 38% of survey participants.

A survey (2025) describes clear fee communication as a competitive advantage and a powerful differentiator, cited by 73% as a priority. Why it might matter: 'Fee structure and pricing' was cited by 61.8% of respondents as the most helpful information when looking for a financial advisor.

A Wealthtender study of higher-income, decision-making adults (August 13, 2025) found that fee transparency is the highest-impact priority (73%) for advisors to address, and that economic stress might increase the importance of fee sensitivity. Why it might matter: the study also recommends online reputation (83% research reputation), response time (50% expect 24-48 hour response), and specialization clarity (64% want specialization info) as priorities.

The Wealthtender study (August 13, 2025) found that consumers prioritize fee transparency when selecting an advisor and expect good advisors to be transparent about their fees. Why it might matter: consumers are advised to plan to contact 2-3 advisors or more to compare options.

Vanguard research (June 4, 2025) found that for digital advice, key client attributes include the need for transparency (visibility of portfolio changes, fee awareness) and empowerment. Why it might matter: for human advice, value is mostly derived from a client's relationship with their financial advisor, whereas digital advice attributes differ.

Cerulli (May 28, 2025) reports fee-based planning is the most preferred form of compensating an advisor among affluent investors, preferred by 36%. Why it might matter: clients have responded well to this shift given that their compensation is tied to portfolio performance rather than to selling particular products.

Why it might matter: among investors with more than $1 million in investable assets, the share willing to pay a premium of 100 basis points or more grew by 50 percent.

Schwab's CEO (2Q25 earnings call, July 18, 2025) states the firm has been a leader in innovation for 50 years, always working alongside regulators in a way that creates transparency and low-cost, effective markets.

Schwab's CEO (3Q26 earnings call, October 15, 2026) states the firm makes it very easy and transparent for clients to see how much cash they hold and what other ways they could invest it, and that it will innovate around helping clients make those decisions.

Merrill (ADV, October 30, 2026) discloses that receipt of data analytics fees from third-party firms creates conflicts of interest, giving it a financial incentive to make available and recommend products from firms that pay such fees.

Raymond James' CEO (1Q26 earnings call, April 22, 2026) states the firm wants a profitable, competitive and fair pricing structure for clients, financial professionals and the firm, and would be flexible and open to evolving with where the industry's clients and advisors are heading.

Merrill (ADV, October 30, 2026) states client assets in its Program are generally invested in the lowest cost eligible mutual fund share class, and that its advisors have no incentive to recommend higher-expense share classes because their compensation is not affected by share class selection.

Trade press (September 29, 2026) reports Merrill Lynch is creating new revenue-sharing support fees and data/shelf fees for third-party asset managers to pay, with the support fee costing up to $1 million per $1 billion of assets managed on behalf of Merrill advisors, ranging from 0.02% on high-net-worth assets to a maximum 0.1% on third-party mutual funds, money market funds, and active ETFs.
Trade press (September 29, 2026) reports Merrill Lynch is a laggard on data fees, being later than many of its peers which have sold advisor data for years, according to analyst Greg O'Gara.
Trade press (September 29, 2026) reports Schwab was an early adopter (leading) on data fees, having introduced data fees over seven years ago.
Trade press (September 29, 2026) reports major wirehouses UBS and Wells Fargo introduced data fees in the mid-2010s and 2020, respectively, earlier than Merrill Lynch.

Trade press (October 16, 2026) reports Wells Fargo and Merrill Lynch agreed to a combined $4.4 million settlement with state securities regulators over charges of unreasonable commissions on small-dollar retail equity transactions (more than 256,000 transactions over a five-year period).

On the question of which firms are leading or lagging on fee structure changes and transparency, the comparison cannot be reliably made on this evidence: the definitions and bases are not unified across firms (fee-structure changes and transparency are reported as qualitative statements, unverified metrics, and firm-specific disclosures with differing scopes, periods, and quantities), so firms cannot be ranked on a single common basis. However, the evidence does contain directional, same-basis signals on data-fee timing: trade press (September 29, 2026) reports Schwab introduced data fees over seven years ago (an early adopter/leading), and that Merrill Lynch is later than many peers on data fees (a laggard).
